## PR Description

Closes #1507
## gh-1507: Boot-path main-isolate hang — boot watchdog + boot-step breadcrumbs

### Root Cause
TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch (iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) with no crash log. The freeze signature matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads) before `runApp`, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs more awaited main-isolate disk reads behind the boot spinner. With only a screenshot report and no sysdiagnose, the exact wedged step was unidentifiable — and the reporting build was 12 versions behind main because the TestFlight leg was failing (#1472, fixed in #1482).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` (new): `BootSteps` — a process-wide boot-step ledger (step name + uptime, in-flight step tracking); `BootWatchdog` — fires a diagnostic breadcrumb if the first frame does not land within the threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS=` override, `0` disables), then re-fires every 30 s until the first frame; a late first frame logs the recovery with uptime and firing count. Breadcrumbs ride the existing `debugPrint` tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb trail).
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/app_boot.dart`: watchdog installed right after the window stage in `run()`/`runWithEnv()`; step marks at every stage boundary and around every persisted store load in `loadBootStores`.
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`: step marks around the post-frame restore (`restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session`) so a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable.
- Boot-path audit (AC2): pre-frame work is inherent to the staged await boot; network surfaces are already non-blocking or guarded (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, 180 s provider connect watchdog). No blind deferrals — moving store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.

### Test Coverage
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (new, 9 tests): ledger ordering/in-flight/cap, threshold firing, 30 s repeat, first-frame cancel, late-frame recovery line, install idempotency — all PASS.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/` — 26/26 PASS.
- CI subset (323 files: non-golden, non-`cli_visual`, `--exclude-tags integration`): 3678 passed, 108 skipped, 2 failed — both in `providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart`, caused by `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` leaking into this runner's shell env (they pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, 10/10; CI does not set the var). Golden/`cli_visual` failures in an unfiltered local run are host-locked per the ci.yml golden comment.

### Notes
- Cannot repro on an iOS device from this environment; the build-gap statement (AC1) stands on the stale-TestFlight-build root (#1472/#1482). Next stale freeze will carry the exact boot step in Crashlytics breadcrumbs / debug logs.
- Behavior is additive-only; the watchdog never changes boot semantics.

- **Title**: gh-1507 [BUG] TestFlight: app freezes ~3s after launch (1.0.536/216, iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) — boot-path main-isolate hang
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1507` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +629
- **Deletions**: -22
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T18:58:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T07:53:22Z

## PR Description

Closes #1507
## gh-1507: Boot-path main-isolate hang — boot watchdog + boot-step breadcrumbs

### Root Cause
TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch (iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) with no crash log. The freeze signature matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads) before `runApp`, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs more awaited main-isolate disk reads behind the boot spinner. With only a screenshot report and no sysdiagnose, the exact wedged step was unidentifiable — and the reporting build was 12 versions behind main because the TestFlight leg was failing (#1472, fixed in #1482).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` (new): `BootSteps` — a process-wide boot-step ledger (step name + uptime, in-flight step tracking); `BootWatchdog` — fires a diagnostic breadcrumb if the first frame does not land within the threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS=` override, `0` disables), then re-fires every 30 s until the first frame; a late first frame logs the recovery with uptime and firing count. Breadcrumbs ride the existing `debugPrint` tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb trail).
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/app_boot.dart`: watchdog installed right after the window stage in `run()`/`runWithEnv()`; step marks at every stage boundary and around every persisted store load in `loadBootStores`.
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`: step marks around the post-frame restore (`restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session`) so a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable.
- Boot-path audit (AC2): pre-frame work is inherent to the staged await boot; network surfaces are already non-blocking or guarded (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, 180 s provider connect watchdog). No blind deferrals — moving store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.

### Test Coverage
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (new, 9 tests): ledger ordering/in-flight/cap, threshold firing, 30 s repeat, first-frame cancel, late-frame recovery line, install idempotency — all PASS.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/` — 26/26 PASS.
- CI subset (323 files: non-golden, non-`cli_visual`, `--exclude-tags integration`): 3678 passed, 108 skipped, 2 failed — both in `providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart`, caused by `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` leaking into this runner's shell env (they pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, 10/10; CI does not set the var). Golden/`cli_visual` failures in an unfiltered local run are host-locked per the ci.yml golden comment.

### Notes
- Cannot repro on an iOS device from this environment; the build-gap statement (AC1) stands on the stale-TestFlight-build root (#1472/#1482). Next stale freeze will carry the exact boot step in Crashlytics breadcrumbs / debug logs.
- Behavior is additive-only; the watchdog never changes boot semantics.

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1507` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +629
- **Deletions**: -22
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T18:58:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T07:53:22Z

## PR Description

Closes #1507
## gh-1507: Boot-path main-isolate hang — boot watchdog + boot-step breadcrumbs

### Root Cause
TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch (iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) with no crash log. The freeze signature matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads) before `runApp`, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs more awaited main-isolate disk reads behind the boot spinner. With only a screenshot report and no sysdiagnose, the exact wedged step was unidentifiable — and the reporting build was 12 versions behind main because the TestFlight leg was failing (#1472, fixed in #1482).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` (new): `BootSteps` — a process-wide boot-step ledger (step name + uptime, in-flight step tracking); `BootWatchdog` — fires a diagnostic breadcrumb if the first frame does not land within the threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS=` override, `0` disables), then re-fires every 30 s until the first frame; a late first frame logs the recovery with uptime and firing count. Breadcrumbs ride the existing `debugPrint` tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb trail).
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/app_boot.dart`: watchdog installed right after the window stage in `run()`/`runWithEnv()`; step marks at every stage boundary and around every persisted store load in `loadBootStores`.
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`: step marks around the post-frame restore (`restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session`) so a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable.
- Boot-path audit (AC2): pre-frame work is inherent to the staged await boot; network surfaces are already non-blocking or guarded (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, 180 s provider connect watchdog). No blind deferrals — moving store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.

### Test Coverage
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (new, 9 tests): ledger ordering/in-flight/cap, threshold firing, 30 s repeat, first-frame cancel, late-frame recovery line, install idempotency — all PASS.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/` — 26/26 PASS.
- CI subset (323 files: non-golden, non-`cli_visual`, `--exclude-tags integration`): 3678 passed, 108 skipped, 2 failed — both in `providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart`, caused by `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` leaking into this runner's shell env (they pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, 10/10; CI does not set the var). Golden/`cli_visual` failures in an unfiltered local run are host-locked per the ci.yml golden comment.

### Notes
- Cannot repro on an iOS device from this environment; the build-gap statement (AC1) stands on the stale-TestFlight-build root (#1472/#1482). Next stale freeze will carry the exact boot step in Crashlytics breadcrumbs / debug logs.
- Behavior is additive-only; the watchdog never changes boot semantics.

  quality-gate:
    name: Quality gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, flutter-analyze, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, usage-fold, cli-visual-settings, cube-kernel-live, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env, fa-aot-build, pty-integration-linux, pty-coverage-gate, pty-visual, supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-verify, install-pin-gate, flutter-app-exzone, flutter-app-lock-smoke]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # #1368: the publish job consumes dart_ok — the pure-Dart package verdict
    # — instead of this aggregate's result. The aggregate itself stays the
    # single required check: any red leg (platform included) still fails it.
    outputs:
      dart_ok: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.dart_ok }}
    steps:
      - name: Report leg results
        run: |
          echo "static        = ${{ needs.static.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "test-core     = ${{ needs.test-core.result }}"
          echo "coverage-gate = ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "guards        = ${{ needs.guards.result }}"
          echo "flutter-analyze = ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}"
          echo "flutter-tests = ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}"
          echo "test-faui     = ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}"
          echo "app-crap-gate = ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}"
          echo "perf-gate     = ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}"
          echo "usage-fold    = ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}"
          echo "cube-live     = ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}"
          echo "cli-visual    = ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}"
          echo "build-web     = ${{ needs.build-web.result }}"
          echo "build-android = ${{ needs.build-android.result }}"
          echo "build-ios     = ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}"
          echo "build-macos   = ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}"
          echo "integ-mock    = ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "pty-integ-linux = ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}"
          echo "fa-aot-build  = ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}"
          echo "pty-gates     = ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "pty-visual    = ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}"
          echo "supply-chain  = ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}"
          echo "dep-audit     = ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}"
          echo "installer-it = ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}"
          echo "pin-gate    = ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}"
          echo "exzone      = ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}"
          echo "lock-smoke  = ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}"
      - name: Fail on any real failure (skipped security = dodge = FAIL)
        id: gate
        env:
          R_CHANGES: ${{ needs.changes.result }}
          R_SUPPLY_CHAIN: ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}
          R_DEP_AUDIT: ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}
          R_STATIC: ${{ needs.static.result }}
          R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE: ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}
          R_TEST_CORE: ${{ needs.test-core.result }}
          R_COVERAGE: ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}
          R_GUARDS: ${{ needs.guards.result }}
          R_FLUTTER: ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}
          R_CRAP: ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}
          R_FAUI: ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}
          R_PERF: ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}
          R_USAGE_FOLD: ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}
          R_CUBE: ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}
          R_CLI_VISUAL: ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}
          R_BUILD_WEB: ${{ needs.build-web.result }}
          R_BUILD_ANDROID: ${{ needs.build-android.result }}
          R_BUILD_IOS: ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}
          R_BUILD_MACOS: ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}
          R_INTEG: ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}
          R_HOSTILE: ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}
          R_PTY_LINUX: ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}
          R_FA_AOT: ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}
          R_PTY_GATES: ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}
          R_PTY_VISUAL: ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}
          R_INSTALLER_VERIFY: ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}
          R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE: ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}
          R_EXZONE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}
          R_LOCK_SMOKE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}
        run: |
          fail() { echo "Quality gate FAILED: $1"; exit 1; }
          # Verdict pass collects blockers WITHOUT exiting, so dart_ok is
          # always exported explicitly ('true' or 'false', never '') —
          # publish and the Provider smoke read this output and an empty
          # value must never read as either (review thread on #1370).
          dart_blocker=""
          # The classifier itself must have run: a failed or skipped
          # classifier skips EVERY downstream leg and would wave a PR
          # through with zero gates executed.
          [ "$R_CHANGES" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="changes classifier = $R_CHANGES"
          # Security legs must EXECUTE and pass. For these, skipped is a
          # dodge (e.g. a cunning diff that makes the classifier misfire),
          # not a pass — review follow-up, #796/#801.
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_SUPPLY_CHAIN" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="supply-chain = $R_SUPPLY_CHAIN (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then

          fi

          #     gate dart_ok AND the aggregate — analyze/test/coverage must

                    "cli-visual-settings:$R_CLI_VISUAL" "build-web:$R_BUILD_WEB" \

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1509
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1509
- **Title**: gh-1507 [BUG] TestFlight: app freezes ~3s after launch (1.0.536/216, iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) — boot-path main-isolate hang
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1507` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +629
- **Deletions**: -22
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T18:58:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T07:53:22Z

## PR Description

Closes #1507
## gh-1507: Boot-path main-isolate hang — boot watchdog + boot-step breadcrumbs

### Root Cause
TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch (iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) with no crash log. The freeze signature matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads) before `runApp`, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs more awaited main-isolate disk reads behind the boot spinner. With only a screenshot report and no sysdiagnose, the exact wedged step was unidentifiable — and the reporting build was 12 versions behind main because the TestFlight leg was failing (#1472, fixed in #1482).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` (new): `BootSteps` — a process-wide boot-step ledger (step name + uptime, in-flight step tracking); `BootWatchdog` — fires a diagnostic breadcrumb if the first frame does not land within the threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS=` override, `0` disables), then re-fires every 30 s until the first frame; a late first frame logs the recovery with uptime and firing count. Breadcrumbs ride the existing `debugPrint` tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb trail).
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/app_boot.dart`: watchdog installed right after the window stage in `run()`/`runWithEnv()`; step marks at every stage boundary and around every persisted store load in `loadBootStores`.
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`: step marks around the post-frame restore (`restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session`) so a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable.
- Boot-path audit (AC2): pre-frame work is inherent to the staged await boot; network surfaces are already non-blocking or guarded (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, 180 s provider connect watchdog). No blind deferrals — moving store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.

### Test Coverage

## Description

- Build: **1.0.536 (216)** — 12 versions behind main (1.0.548); the TestFlight leg has been failing (#1472), so testers run stale builds
- Device: iPhone16,1 (iPhone 15 Pro), iOS 27.0.1, arm64e, Wi-Fi, disk 3.4 GB free of 114 GB, battery 40%

Boot-path main-isolate work to audit for blocking IO / unawaited deadlocks:

flutter-tests:
    name: Flutter app tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    # End-of-run drain can stall minutes under shared-runner load while
    # every test already passed (0 failures, killed mid-drain on #330):
    # fa_ui shards get 12m and flutter_app is the heaviest package.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Bootstrap via git
      # clone instead: flutter_tools pulls the official arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # See flutter-analyze: placeholder must exist before pub get.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Golden suite is intentionally NOT here: goldens are host-locked
      # (same macOS host renders them differently across minor SDKs — see the
      # dynamic_messages saga) and would all redden on ubuntu. Widget/unit
      # tests run here on a cheap runner; goldens stay guarded by
      # build-macos.yml and the nightly full matrix (issue #177 E5/OQ3:
      # pinned-font golden migration is a follow-up, not this card).
      - name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
        # Goldens stay out (host-locked, see the golden comment above).
        # Native-dependent tests (quickjs_c_bridge .so, mic channel) are NOT
        # excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in
        # flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart + the injected-ASR fix.
        # Deterministic modulo split of the sorted file list: shard i takes
        # lines where NR % 2 == i — union == the old single job's list.
        run: |
          cd flutter_app
          find test -name '*_test.dart' ! -path '*/golden/*' ! -path '*/cli_visual/*' \
            | sort | awk -v i=${{ matrix.shard }} 'NR % 2 == i' > shard-files.txt
          echo "shard files: $(wc -l < shard-files.txt)"
          # --coverage (issue #433): each shard emits lcov for the
          # app-crap-gate job; the covered surface matches the CRAP
          # sources [lib] exactly.
          flutter test --exclude-tags integration --coverage $(cat shard-files.txt)

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: app-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

      # Issue #239 AC3: the App Store submission pre-flight matrix is plain
      # ruby over flutter_app/fastlane/appstore_preflight.rb — no gems,
      # runs in under a second on the runner's stock ruby.
      # Issue #289 adds the fastlane guard/preflight suites (android id
      # guard + Play upload pre-flight) — same plain-ruby contract, so the
      # step loops over every fastlane test file. Shard 0 only: once is
      # enough (fa PR #333).
      - name: Fastlane pre-flight suites (ruby)
        if: matrix.shard == 0
        run: |
          for t in flutter_app/fastlane/test/*_test.rb; do
            echo "::group::ruby $t"
            ruby "$t"
            echo "::endgroup::"
          done

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #1267 N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg. By #177 design the ubuntu
  # PR leg never EXERCISES the JS-engine suites: flutter_app/test/apps/**
  # skip their engine-dependent tests on ubuntu (native_test_guard.dart
  # finds no QuickJS .so on a bare runner), so that surface ran only in the
  # nightly macOS leg — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an
  # apps/engine regression merged green and went red the same night).
  #
  # Trigger model (issue #1267 N1 slice 2): ci.yml has NO pull_request
  # trigger — PR validation arrives as an SM workflow_dispatch on the head
  # SHA (machine-sm.yml). The changes classifier derives the validated diff
  # under BOTH events (merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) on dispatches), so
  # this leg is PATH-TRIGGERED: a PR touching only lib/src core never pays
  # for it (AC1), a lib/apps + js_ext diff does, and a classifier failure
  # fails safe (the leg runs). Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it —
  # gh-1538 retired the nightly flutter-app-macos full-suite backstop
  # (nightly is builds + integration-only now), so this pre-merge leg is
  # the macOS coverage for the JS-engine surface.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-exzone:
    name: Exclusion zone (macOS JS-engine tests)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true' &&
      needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 25

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1509
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1509
- **Title**: gh-1507 [BUG] TestFlight: app freezes ~3s after launch (1.0.536/216, iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) — boot-path main-isolate hang
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1507` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +629
- **Deletions**: -22
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T18:58:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T07:53:22Z

## PR Description

Closes #1507
## gh-1507: Boot-path main-isolate hang — boot watchdog + boot-step breadcrumbs

### Root Cause
TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch (iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) with no crash log. The freeze signature matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads) before `runApp`, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs more awaited main-isolate disk reads behind the boot spinner. With only a screenshot report and no sysdiagnose, the exact wedged step was unidentifiable — and the reporting build was 12 versions behind main because the TestFlight leg was failing (#1472, fixed in #1482).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` (new): `BootSteps` — a process-wide boot-step ledger (step name + uptime, in-flight step tracking); `BootWatchdog` — fires a diagnostic breadcrumb if the first frame does not land within the threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS=` override, `0` disables), then re-fires every 30 s until the first frame; a late first frame logs the recovery with uptime and firing count. Breadcrumbs ride the existing `debugPrint` tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb trail).
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/app_boot.dart`: watchdog installed right after the window stage in `run()`/`runWithEnv()`; step marks at every stage boundary and around every persisted store load in `loadBootStores`.
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`: step marks around the post-frame restore (`restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session`) so a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable.
- Boot-path audit (AC2): pre-frame work is inherent to the staged await boot; network surfaces are already non-blocking or guarded (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, 180 s provider connect watchdog). No blind deferrals — moving store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.

### Test Coverage
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (new, 9 tests): ledger ordering/in-flight/cap, threshold firing, 30 s repeat, first-frame cancel, late-frame recovery line, install idempotency — all PASS.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/` — 26/26 PASS.
- CI subset (323 files: non-golden, non-`cli_visual`, `--exclude-tags integration`): 3678 passed, 108 skipped, 2 failed — both in `providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart`, caused by `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` leaking into this runner's shell env (they pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, 10/10; CI does not set the var). Golden/`cli_visual` failures in an unfiltered local run are host-locked per the ci.yml golden comment.

### Notes
- Cannot repro on an iOS device from this environment; the build-gap statement (AC1) stands on the stale-TestFlight-build root (#1472/#1482). Next stale freeze will carry the exact boot step in Crashlytics breadcrumbs / debug logs.
- Behavior is additive-only; the watchdog never changes boot semantics.

# gh-1507: [BUG] TestFlight: app freezes ~3s after launch (1.0.536/216, iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) — boot-path main-isolate hang

## Description

## TestFlight feedback (raw: feedback.json, no crash log attached)

- **Report**: "Just freezed" — app uptime **3000 ms** at report time (freeze ~3s after launch, i.e. during boot)
- Build: **1.0.536 (216)** — 12 versions behind main (1.0.548); the TestFlight leg has been failing (#1472), so testers run stale builds
- Device: iPhone16,1 (iPhone 15 Pro), iOS 27.0.1, arm64e, Wi-Fi, disk 3.4 GB free of 114 GB, battery 40%

Not a crash (no .ips attached) — a **hang/freeze during startup**, i.e. main-isolate block or deadlock in the boot path.

## Suspects (boot path, first ~3s)

Boot-path main-isolate work to audit for blocking IO / unawaited deadlocks:
1. Session/keys restore (`SessionKeysStore`, folder model pin restore)
2. Memory index / Obsidian vault scan at boot
3. Messaging fabric watcher + unified-root migration (`~/.fah/messages`)
4. Any synchronous network call before first frame (provider catalog fetch — the 180s connect watchdog covers provider streams, NOT app boot fetches)
5. JS/widget engine warmup, on-device model init (gemma/webllm lazy?)

## Acceptance

1. Repro attempt on current main build (1.0.548+) — cold start on iOS device, watch for boot hang; if unreproducible on current build, state which change since 1.0.536 plausibly fixed it.
2. Boot-path audit: no blocking IO on the main isolate before first frame; every boot fetch has a timeout; heavy init deferred post-frame.
3. Add a boot watchdog: if first frame takes > N sec, log a diagnostic breadcrumb (uptime, last completed boot step) so the next TestFlight feedback is actionable without guessing.

## Notes

- Raw feedback: `feedback.json` only (TestFlight screenshot feedback without sysdiagnose). Device owner = developer (istin2007@gmail.com), so a sysdiagnose / repro is obtainable on request.
- Unblocks together with the TestFlight leg fix (#1477, merged in #1482 — first green daily with it expected 2026-10-11 ~05:30Z).

blocks.text:
flutter-tests:
    name: Flutter app tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    # End-of-run drain can stall minutes under shared-runner load while
    # every test already passed (0 failures, killed mid-drain on #330):
    # fa_ui shards get 12m and flutter_app is the heaviest package.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Bootstrap via git
      # clone instead: flutter_tools pulls the official arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # See flutter-analyze: placeholder must exist before pub get.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Golden suite is intentionally NOT here: goldens are host-locked
      # (same macOS host renders them differently across minor SDKs — see the
      # dynamic_messages saga) and would all redden on ubuntu. Widget/unit
      # tests run here on a cheap runner; goldens stay guarded by
      # build-macos.yml and the nightly full matrix (issue #177 E5/OQ3:
      # pinned-font golden migration is a follow-up, not this card).
      - name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
        # Goldens stay out (host-locked, see the golden comment above).
        # Native-dependent tests (quickjs_c_bridge .so, mic channel) are NOT
        # excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in
        # flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart + the injected-ASR fix.
        # Deterministic modulo split of the sorted file list: shard i takes
        # lines where NR % 2 == i — union == the old single job's list.
        run: |
          cd flutter_app
          find test -name '*_test.dart' ! -path '*/golden/*' ! -path '*/cli_visual/*' \
            | sort | awk -v i=${{ matrix.shard }} 'NR % 2 == i' > shard-files.txt
          echo "shard files: $(wc -l < shard-files.txt)"
          # --coverage (issue #433): each shard emits lcov for the
          # app-crap-gate job; the covered surface matches the CRAP
          # sources [lib] exactly.
          flutter test --exclude-tags integration --coverage $(cat shard-files.txt)

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: app-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

      # Issue #239 AC3: the App Store submission pre-flight matrix is plain
      # ruby over flutter_app/fastlane/appstore_preflight.rb — no gems,
      # runs in under a second on the runner's stock ruby.
      # Issue #289 adds the fastlane guard/preflight suites (android id
      # guard + Play upload pre-flight) — same plain-ruby contract, so the
      # step loops over every fastlane test file. Shard 0 only: once is
      # enough (fa PR #333).
      - name: Fastlane pre-flight suites (ruby)
        if: matrix.shard == 0
        run: |
          for t in flutter_app/fastlane/test/*_test.rb; do
            echo "::group::ruby $t"
            ruby "$t"
            echo "::endgroup::"
          done

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #1267 N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg. By #177 design the ubuntu
  # PR leg never EXERCISES the JS-engine suites: flutter_app/test/apps/**
  # skip their engine-dependent tests on ubuntu (native_test_guard.dart
  # finds no QuickJS .so on a bare runner), so that surface ran only in the
  # nightly macOS leg — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an
  # apps/engine regression merged green and went red the same night).
  #
  # Trigger model (issue #1267 N1 slice 2): ci.yml has NO pull_request
  # trigger — PR validation arrives as an SM workflow_dispatch on the head
  # SHA (machine-sm.yml). The changes classifier derives the validated diff
  # under BOTH events (merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) on dispatches), so
  # this leg is PATH-TRIGGERED: a PR touching only lib/src core never pays
  # for it (AC1), a lib/apps + js_ext diff does, and a classifier failure
  # fails safe (the leg runs). Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it —
  # gh-1538 retired the nightly flutter-app-macos full-suite backstop
  # (nightly is builds + integration-only now), so this pre-merge leg is
  # the macOS coverage for the JS-engine surface.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-exzone:
    name: Exclusion zone (macOS JS-engine tests)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true' &&
      needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 25

- **PR #**: 1509
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1509
- **Title**: gh-1507 [BUG] TestFlight: app freezes ~3s after launch (1.0.536/216, iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) — boot-path main-isolate hang
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1507` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +629
- **Deletions**: -22
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T18:58:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T07:53:22Z

## PR Description

Closes #1507
## gh-1507: Boot-path main-isolate hang — boot watchdog + boot-step breadcrumbs

### Root Cause
TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch (iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) with no crash log. The freeze signature matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads) before `runApp`, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs more awaited main-isolate disk reads behind the boot spinner. With only a screenshot report and no sysdiagnose, the exact wedged step was unidentifiable — and the reporting build was 12 versions behind main because the TestFlight leg was failing (#1472, fixed in #1482).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` (new): `BootSteps` — a process-wide boot-step ledger (step name + uptime, in-flight step tracking); `BootWatchdog` — fires a diagnostic breadcrumb if the first frame does not land within the threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS=` override, `0` disables), then re-fires every 30 s until the first frame; a late first frame logs the recovery with uptime and firing count. Breadcrumbs ride the existing `debugPrint` tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb trail).
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/app_boot.dart`: watchdog installed right after the window stage in `run()`/`runWithEnv()`; step marks at every stage boundary and around every persisted store load in `loadBootStores`.
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`: step marks around the post-frame restore (`restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session`) so a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable.
- Boot-path audit (AC2): pre-frame work is inherent to the staged await boot; network surfaces are already non-blocking or guarded (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, 180 s provider connect watchdog). blocks.text:
flutter-tests:
    name: Flutter app tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    # End-of-run drain can stall minutes under shared-runner load while
    # every test already passed (0 failures, killed mid-drain on #330):
    # fa_ui shards get 12m and flutter_app is the heaviest package.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Bootstrap via git
      # clone instead: flutter_tools pulls the official arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # See flutter-analyze: placeholder must exist before pub get.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Golden suite is intentionally NOT here: goldens are host-locked
      # (same macOS host renders them differently across minor SDKs — see the
      # dynamic_messages saga) and would all redden on ubuntu. Widget/unit
      # tests run here on a cheap runner; goldens stay guarded by
      # build-macos.yml and the nightly full matrix (issue #177 E5/OQ3:
      # pinned-font golden migration is a follow-up, not this card).
      - name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
        # Goldens stay out (host-locked, see the golden comment above).
        # Native-dependent tests (quickjs_c_bridge .so, mic channel) are NOT
        # excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in
        # flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart + the injected-ASR fix.
        # Deterministic modulo split of the sorted file list: shard i takes
        # lines where NR % 2 == i — union == the old single job's list.
        run: |
          cd flutter_app
          find test -name '*_test.dart' ! -path '*/golden/*' ! -path '*/cli_visual/*' \
            | sort | awk -v i=${{ matrix.shard }} 'NR % 2 == i' > shard-files.txt
          echo "shard files: $(wc -l < shard-files.txt)"
          # --coverage (issue #433): each shard emits lcov for the
          # app-crap-gate job; the covered surface matches the CRAP
          # sources [lib] exactly.
          flutter test --exclude-tags integration --coverage $(cat shard-files.txt)

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: app-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

      # Issue #239 AC3: the App Store submission pre-flight matrix is plain
      # ruby over flutter_app/fastlane/appstore_preflight.rb — no gems,
      # runs in under a second on the runner's stock ruby.
      # Issue #289 adds the fastlane guard/preflight suites (android id
      # guard + Play upload pre-flight) — same plain-ruby contract, so the
      # step loops over every fastlane test file. Shard 0 only: once is
      # enough (fa PR #333).
      - name: Fastlane pre-flight suites (ruby)
        if: matrix.shard == 0
        run: |
          for t in flutter_app/fastlane/test/*_test.rb; do
            echo "::group::ruby $t"
            ruby "$t"
            echo "::endgroup::"
          done

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #1267 N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg. By #177 design the ubuntu
  # PR leg never EXERCISES the JS-engine suites: flutter_app/test/apps/**
  # skip their engine-dependent tests on ubuntu (native_test_guard.dart
  # finds no QuickJS .so on a bare runner), so that surface ran only in the
  # nightly macOS leg — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an
  # apps/engine regression merged green and went red the same night).
  #
  # Trigger model (issue #1267 N1 slice 2): ci.yml has NO pull_request
  # trigger — PR validation arrives as an SM workflow_dispatch on the head
  # SHA (machine-sm.yml). The changes classifier derives the validated diff
  # under BOTH events (merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) on dispatches), so
  # this leg is PATH-TRIGGERED: a PR touching only lib/src core never pays
  # for it (AC1), a lib/apps + js_ext diff does, and a classifier failure
  # fails safe (the leg runs). Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it —
  # gh-1538 retired the nightly flutter-app-macos full-suite backstop
  # (nightly is builds + integration-only now), so this pre-merge leg is
  # the macOS coverage for the JS-engine surface.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-exzone:
    name: Exclusion zone (macOS JS-engine tests)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true' &&
      needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 25

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1509
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1509
- **Title**: gh-1507 [BUG] TestFlight: app freezes ~3s after launch (1.0.536/216, iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) — boot-path main-isolate hang
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1507` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +629
- **Deletions**: -22
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T18:58:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T07:53:22Z

## PR Description

Closes #1507
## gh-1507: Boot-path main-isolate hang — boot watchdog + boot-step breadcrumbs

### Root Cause
TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch (iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) with no crash log. The freeze signature matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads) before `runApp`, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs more awaited main-isolate disk reads behind the boot spinner. With only a screenshot report and no sysdiagnose, the exact wedged step was unidentifiable — and the reporting build was 12 versions behind main because the TestFlight leg was failing (#1472, fixed in #1482).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` (new): `BootSteps` — a process-wide boot-step ledger (step name + uptime, in-flight step tracking); `BootWatchdog` — fires a diagnostic breadcrumb if the first frame does not land within the threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS=` override, `0` disables), then re-fires every 30 s until the first frame; a late first frame logs the recovery with uptime and firing count. Breadcrumbs ride the existing `debugPrint` tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb trail).
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/app_boot.dart`: watchdog installed right after the window stage in `run()`/`runWithEnv()`; step marks at every stage boundary and around every persisted store load in `loadBootStores`.
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`: step marks around the post-frame restore (`restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session`) so a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable.
- Boot-path audit (AC2): pre-frame work is inherent to the staged await boot; network surfaces are already non-blocking or guarded (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, 180 s provider connect watchdog). No blind deferrals — moving store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.

### Test Coverage
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (new, 9 tests): ledger ordering/in-flight/cap, threshold firing, 30 s repeat, first-frame cancel, late-frame recovery line, install idempotency — all PASS.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/` — 26/26 PASS.
- CI subset (323 files: non-golden, non-`cli_visual`, `--exclude-tags integration`): 3678 passed, 108 skipped, 2 failed — both in `providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart`, caused by `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` leaking into this runner's shell env (they pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, 10/10; CI does not set the var). Golden/`cli_visual` failures in an unfiltered local run are host-locked per the ci.yml golden comment.

### Notes
- Cannot repro on an iOS device from this environment; the build-gap statement (AC1) stands on the stale-TestFlight-build root (#1472/#1482). Next stale freeze will carry the exact boot step in Crashlytics breadcrumbs / debug logs.
- Behavior is additive-only; the watchdog never changes boot semantics.

# gh-1507: [BUG] TestFlight: app freezes ~3s after launch (1.0.536/216, iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) — boot-path main-isolate hang

## Description

## TestFlight feedback (raw: feedback.json, no crash log attached)

- **Report**: "Just freezed" — app uptime **3000 ms** at report time (freeze ~3s after launch, i.e. during boot)
- Build: **1.0.536 (216)** — 12 versions behind main (1.0.548); the TestFlight leg has been failing (#1472), so testers run stale builds
- Device: iPhone16,1 (iPhone 15 Pro), iOS 27.0.1, arm64e, Wi-Fi, disk 3.4 GB free of 114 GB, battery 40%

Not a crash (no .ips attached) — a **hang/freeze during startup**, i.e. main-isolate block or deadlock in the boot path.

## Suspects (boot path, first ~3s)

Boot-path main-isolate work to audit for blocking IO / unawaited deadlocks:
1. Session/keys restore (`SessionKeysStore`, folder model pin restore)
2. Memory index / Obsidian vault scan at boot
3. Messaging fabric watcher + unified-root migration (`~/.fah/messages`)
4. Any synchronous network call before first frame (provider catalog fetch — the 180s connect watchdog covers provider streams, NOT app boot fetches)
5. JS/widget engine warmup, on-device model init (gemma/webllm lazy?)

## Acceptance

1. Repro attempt on current main build (1.0.548+) — cold start on iOS device, watch for boot hang; if unreproducible on current build, state which change since 1.0.536 plausibly fixed it.
2. Boot-path audit: no blocking IO on the main isolate before first frame; every boot fetch has a timeout; heavy init deferred post-frame.
3. Add a boot watchdog: if first frame takes > N sec, log a diagnostic breadcrumb (uptime, last completed boot step) so the next TestFlight feedback is actionable without guessing.

## Notes

- Raw feedback: `feedback.json` only (TestFlight screenshot feedback without sysdiagnose). Device owner = developer (istin2007@gmail.com), so a sysdiagnose / repro is obtainable on request.
- Unblocks together with the TestFlight leg fix (#1477, merged in #1482 — first green daily with it expected 2026-10-11 ~05:30Z).

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: The `restore:*` marks are dead weight — a post-frame wedge produces no breadcrumb**

`BootWatchdog.firstFrame()` (called from the first post-frame callback) permanently cancels the timer, and nothing else ever reads `BootSteps.describe()`. So by the time `_BootstrapScreen._boot` runs, the watchdog is already disarmed: if the restore chain (`createPlatformEnv` → `FlutterSessionManager` → `createOrResumeSession`) hangs — the exact "freeze ~3 s after launch, spinner on screen" scenario reported on TestFlight — **zero** breadcrumbs are emitted, and the `restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session` marks sit silently in the ledger.

This contradicts the PR description's claim that "a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable." Two options:

1. Keep the watchdog armed through the restore: cancel on first frame only for the *pre-frame* threshold, then arm a second, restore-scoped timer (e.g. N s without `restore:session` completing → breadcrumb). This is the diagnosability the ticket actually needs, since the reported freeze was at 3 s uptime — plausibly already past the first frame.
2. Drop the `restore:*` marks and correct the PR description.

As written, the marks cost ledger noise and imply coverage that does not exist.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

💡 **SUGGESTION: Document the watchdog's blind spot — a hard-blocked main isolate**

The probe is a `Timer` + `addPostFrameCallback`, so it can only fire when the event loop is alive. If the freeze is caused by *synchronous* main-isolate work (one of the ticket's own suspects: vault scan, messaging-fabric migration, synchronous disk reads), neither the timer nor the post-frame callback ever runs and the breadcrumb never fires — the watchdog would incorrectly look "healthy" during exactly the hang it exists to diagnose. An await-chain deadlock or event-loop starvation is caught; a CPU block is not.

Worth one or two lines in the class doc so the next triage does not over-trust a silent watchdog, e.g.: "Detects stalls where the event loop still turns; a synchronously blocked main isolate suppresses both the probe and the breadcrumb."

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

💡 **SUGGESTION: Bound the repeat firing count**

`_fire()` re-arms unconditionally every 30 s, so a permanently wedged boot (or an app backgrounded mid-boot) logs a breadcrumb forever — one every 30 s for the lifetime of the process. That is fine for a one-shot diagnostic but grows `logs/app.log` and the Crashlytics breadcrumb trail without bound. Consider a cap (e.g. stop after 10 firings with a final "giving up" line, or back off exponentially). Not blocking — the current behavior is defensible if unbounded trail is intentional.

    name: Quality gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, flutter-analyze, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, usage-fold, cli-visual-settings, cube-kernel-live, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env, fa-aot-build, pty-integration-linux, pty-coverage-gate, pty-visual, supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-verify, install-pin-gate, flutter-app-exzone, flutter-app-lock-smoke]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # #1368: the publish job consumes dart_ok — the pure-Dart package verdict
    # — instead of this aggregate's result. The aggregate itself stays the
    # single required check: any red leg (platform included) still fails it.
    outputs:
      dart_ok: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.dart_ok }}
    steps:
      - name: Report leg results
        run: |
          echo "static        = ${{ needs.static.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "test-core     = ${{ needs.test-core.result }}"
          echo "coverage-gate = ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}"

          echo "build-ios     = ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}"
          echo "build-macos   = ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}"

          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "pty-integ-linux = ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}"
          echo "fa-aot-build  = ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}"
          echo "pty-gates     = ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "pty-visual    = ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}"

          echo "installer-it = ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}"
          echo "pin-gate    = ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}"
          echo "exzone      = ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}"
          echo "lock-smoke  = ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}"

        id: gate
        env:
          R_CHANGES: ${{ needs.changes.result }}
          R_SUPPLY_CHAIN: ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}
          R_DEP_AUDIT: ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}
          R_STATIC: ${{ needs.static.result }}
          R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE: ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}
          R_TEST_CORE: ${{ needs.test-core.result }}
          R_COVERAGE: ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}
          R_GUARDS: ${{ needs.guards.result }}
          R_FLUTTER: ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}
          R_CRAP: ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}
          R_FAUI: ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}
          R_PERF: ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}
          R_USAGE_FOLD: ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}
          R_CUBE: ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}
          R_CLI_VISUAL: ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}
          R_BUILD_WEB: ${{ needs.build-web.result }}
          R_BUILD_ANDROID: ${{ needs.build-android.result }}
          R_BUILD_IOS: ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}
          R_BUILD_MACOS: ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}
          R_INTEG: ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}
          R_HOSTILE: ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}
          R_PTY_LINUX: ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}
          R_FA_AOT: ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}
          R_PTY_GATES: ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}
          R_PTY_VISUAL: ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}
          R_INSTALLER_VERIFY: ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}
          R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE: ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}
          R_EXZONE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}
          R_LOCK_SMOKE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}
        run: |
          fail() { echo "Quality gate FAILED: $1"; exit 1; }
          # Verdict pass collects blockers WITHOUT exiting, so dart_ok is
          # always exported explicitly ('true' or 'false', never '') —
          # publish and the Provider smoke read this output and an empty
          # value must never read as either (review thread on #1370).
          dart_blocker=""

          # classifier skips EVERY downstream leg and would wave a PR
          # through with zero gates executed.
          [ "$R_CHANGES" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="changes classifier = $R_CHANGES"

          # dodge (e.g. a cunning diff that makes the classifier misfire),

          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then

blocks.text:
flutter-tests:
    name: Flutter app tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    # End-of-run drain can stall minutes under shared-runner load while
    # every test already passed (0 failures, killed mid-drain on #330):
    # fa_ui shards get 12m and flutter_app is the heaviest package.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Bootstrap via git
      # clone instead: flutter_tools pulls the official arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # See flutter-analyze: placeholder must exist before pub get.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Golden suite is intentionally NOT here: goldens are host-locked
      # (same macOS host renders them differently across minor SDKs — see the
      # dynamic_messages saga) and would all redden on ubuntu. Widget/unit
      # tests run here on a cheap runner; goldens stay guarded by
      # build-macos.yml and the nightly full matrix (issue #177 E5/OQ3:
      # pinned-font golden migration is a follow-up, not this card).
      - name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
        # Goldens stay out (host-locked, see the golden comment above).
        # Native-dependent tests (quickjs_c_bridge .so, mic channel) are NOT
        # excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in
        # flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart + the injected-ASR fix.
        # Deterministic modulo split of the sorted file list: shard i takes
        # lines where NR % 2 == i — union == the old single job's list.
        run: |
          cd flutter_app
          find test -name '*_test.dart' ! -path '*/golden/*' ! -path '*/cli_visual/*' \
            | sort | awk -v i=${{ matrix.shard }} 'NR % 2 == i' > shard-files.txt
          echo "shard files: $(wc -l < shard-files.txt)"
          # --coverage (issue #433): each shard emits lcov for the
          # app-crap-gate job; the covered surface matches the CRAP
          # sources [lib] exactly.
          flutter test --exclude-tags integration --coverage $(cat shard-files.txt)

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: app-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

      # Issue #239 AC3: the App Store submission pre-flight matrix is plain
      # ruby over flutter_app/fastlane/appstore_preflight.rb — no gems,
      # runs in under a second on the runner's stock ruby.
      # Issue #289 adds the fastlane guard/preflight suites (android id
      # guard + Play upload pre-flight) — same plain-ruby contract, so the
      # step loops over every fastlane test file. Shard 0 only: once is
      # enough (fa PR #333).
      - name: Fastlane pre-flight suites (ruby)
        if: matrix.shard == 0
        run: |
          for t in flutter_app/fastlane/test/*_test.rb; do
            echo "::group::ruby $t"
            ruby "$t"
            echo "::endgroup::"
          done

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #1267 N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg. By #177 design the ubuntu
  # PR leg never EXERCISES the JS-engine suites: flutter_app/test/apps/**
  # skip their engine-dependent tests on ubuntu (native_test_guard.dart
  # finds no QuickJS .so on a bare runner), so that surface ran only in the
  # nightly macOS leg — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an
  # apps/engine regression merged green and went red the same night).
  #
  # Trigger model (issue #1267 N1 slice 2): ci.yml has NO pull_request
  # trigger — PR validation arrives as an SM workflow_dispatch on the head
  # SHA (machine-sm.yml). The changes classifier derives the validated diff
  # under BOTH events (merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) on dispatches), so
  # this leg is PATH-TRIGGERED: a PR touching only lib/src core never pays
  # for it (AC1), a lib/apps + js_ext diff does, and a classifier failure
  # fails safe (the leg runs). Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it —
  # gh-1538 retired the nightly flutter-app-macos full-suite backstop
  # (nightly is builds + integration-only now), so this pre-merge leg is
  # the macOS coverage for the JS-engine surface.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-exzone:
    name: Exclusion zone (macOS JS-engine tests)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true' &&
      needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 25

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1507` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +629
- **Deletions**: -22
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T18:58:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T07:53:22Z

## PR Description

Closes #1507
## gh-1507: Boot-path main-isolate hang — boot watchdog + boot-step breadcrumbs

### Root Cause
TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch (iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) with no crash log. The freeze signature matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads) before `runApp`, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs more awaited main-isolate disk reads behind the boot spinner. With only a screenshot report and no sysdiagnose, the exact wedged step was unidentifiable — and the reporting build was 12 versions behind main because the TestFlight leg was failing (#1472, fixed in #1482).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` (new): `BootSteps` — a process-wide boot-step ledger (step name + uptime, in-flight step tracking); `BootWatchdog` — fires a diagnostic breadcrumb if the first frame does not land within the threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS=` override, `0` disables), then re-fires every 30 s until the first frame; a late first frame logs the recovery with uptime and firing count. Breadcrumbs ride the existing `debugPrint` tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb trail).
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/app_boot.dart`: watchdog installed right after the window stage in `run()`/`runWithEnv()`; step marks at every stage boundary and around every persisted store load in `loadBootStores`.
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`: step marks around the post-frame restore (`restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session`) so a wedge after the first frame is equally diagnosable.
- Boot-path audit (AC2): pre-frame work is inherent to the staged await boot; network surfaces are already non-blocking or guarded (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, 180 s provider connect watchdog). No blind deferrals — moving store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.

### Test Coverage
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (new, 9 tests): ledger ordering/in-flight/cap, threshold firing, 30 s repeat, first-frame cancel, late-frame recovery line, install idempotency — all PASS.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/` — 26/26 PASS.
- CI subset (323 files: non-golden, non-`cli_visual`, `--exclude-tags integration`): 3678 passed, 108 skipped, 2 failed — both in `providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart`, caused by `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` leaking into this runner's shell env (they pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, 10/10; CI does not set the var). Golden/`cli_visual` failures in an unfiltered local run are host-locked per the ci.yml golden comment.

### Notes
- Cannot repro on an iOS device from this environment; the build-gap statement (AC1) stands on the stale-TestFlight-build root (#1472/#1482). Next stale freeze will carry the exact boot step in Crashlytics breadcrumbs / debug logs.
- Behavior is additive-only; the watchdog never changes boot semantics.

  quality-gate:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, flutter-analyze, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, usage-fold, cli-visual-settings, cube-kernel-live, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env, fa-aot-build, pty-integration-linux, pty-coverage-gate, pty-visual, supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-verify, install-pin-gate, flutter-app-exzone, flutter-app-lock-smoke]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # #1368: the publish job consumes dart_ok — the pure-Dart package verdict
    # — instead of this aggregate's result. The aggregate itself stays the
    # single required check: any red leg (platform included) still fails it.
    outputs:
      dart_ok: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.dart_ok }}
    steps:
      - name: Report leg results
        run: |
          echo "static        = ${{ needs.static.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "test-core     = ${{ needs.test-core.result }}"
          echo "coverage-gate = ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}"

          echo "cli-visual    = ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}"
          echo "build-web     = ${{ needs.build-web.result }}"
          echo "build-android = ${{ needs.build-android.result }}"
          echo "build-ios     = ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}"
          echo "build-macos   = ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}"
          echo "integ-mock    = ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "pty-integ-linux = ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}"
          echo "fa-aot-build  = ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}"

          echo "exzone      = ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}"
          echo "lock-smoke  = ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}"
      - name: Fail on any real failure (skipped security = dodge = FAIL)
        id: gate
        env:
          R_CHANGES: ${{ needs.changes.result }}
          R_SUPPLY_CHAIN: ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}
          R_DEP_AUDIT: ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}
          R_STATIC: ${{ needs.static.result }}
          R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE: ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}
          R_TEST_CORE: ${{ needs.test-core.result }}
          R_COVERAGE: ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}
          R_GUARDS: ${{ needs.guards.result }}
          R_FLUTTER: ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}
          R_CRAP: ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}
          R_FAUI: ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}
          R_PERF: ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}
          R_USAGE_FOLD: ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}
          R_CUBE: ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}
          R_CLI_VISUAL: ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}
          R_BUILD_WEB: ${{ needs.build-web.result }}
          R_BUILD_ANDROID: ${{ needs.build-android.result }}
          R_BUILD_IOS: ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}
          R_BUILD_MACOS: ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}
          R_INTEG: ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}
          R_HOSTILE: ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}
          R_PTY_LINUX: ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}
          R_FA_AOT: ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}
          R_PTY_GATES: ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}
          R_PTY_VISUAL: ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}
          R_INSTALLER_VERIFY: ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}
          R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE: ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}
          R_EXZONE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}
          R_LOCK_SMOKE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}
        run: |

blocks.text:
flutter-tests:
    name: Flutter app tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    # End-of-run drain can stall minutes under shared-runner load while
    # every test already passed (0 failures, killed mid-drain on #330):
    # fa_ui shards get 12m and flutter_app is the heaviest package.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Bootstrap via git
      # clone instead: flutter_tools pulls the official arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # See flutter-analyze: placeholder must exist before pub get.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Golden suite is intentionally NOT here: goldens are host-locked
      # (same macOS host renders them differently across minor SDKs — see the
      # dynamic_messages saga) and would all redden on ubuntu. Widget/unit
      # tests run here on a cheap runner; goldens stay guarded by
      # build-macos.yml and the nightly full matrix (issue #177 E5/OQ3:
      # pinned-font golden migration is a follow-up, not this card).
      - name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
        # Goldens stay out (host-locked, see the golden comment above).
        # Native-dependent tests (quickjs_c_bridge .so, mic channel) are NOT
        # excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in
        # flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart + the injected-ASR fix.
        # Deterministic modulo split of the sorted file list: shard i takes
        # lines where NR % 2 == i — union == the old single job's list.
        run: |
          cd flutter_app
          find test -name '*_test.dart' ! -path '*/golden/*' ! -path '*/cli_visual/*' \
            | sort | awk -v i=${{ matrix.shard }} 'NR % 2 == i' > shard-files.txt
          echo "shard files: $(wc -l < shard-files.txt)"
          # --coverage (issue #433): each shard emits lcov for the
          # app-crap-gate job; the covered surface matches the CRAP
          # sources [lib] exactly.
          flutter test --exclude-tags integration --coverage $(cat shard-files.txt)

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: app-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

      # Issue #239 AC3: the App Store submission pre-flight matrix is plain
      # ruby over flutter_app/fastlane/appstore_preflight.rb — no gems,
      # runs in under a second on the runner's stock ruby.
      # Issue #289 adds the fastlane guard/preflight suites (android id
      # guard + Play upload pre-flight) — same plain-ruby contract, so the
      # step loops over every fastlane test file. Shard 0 only: once is
      # enough (fa PR #333).
      - name: Fastlane pre-flight suites (ruby)
        if: matrix.shard == 0
        run: |
          for t in flutter_app/fastlane/test/*_test.rb; do
            echo "::group::ruby $t"
            ruby "$t"
            echo "::endgroup::"
          done

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #1267 N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg. By #177 design the ubuntu
  # PR leg never EXERCISES the JS-engine suites: flutter_app/test/apps/**
  # skip their engine-dependent tests on ubuntu (native_test_guard.dart
  # finds no QuickJS .so on a bare runner), so that surface ran only in the
  # nightly macOS leg — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an
  # apps/engine regression merged green and went red the same night).
  #
  # Trigger model (issue #1267 N1 slice 2): ci.yml has NO pull_request
  # trigger — PR validation arrives as an SM workflow_dispatch on the head
  # SHA (machine-sm.yml). The changes classifier derives the validated diff
  # under BOTH events (merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) on dispatches), so
  # this leg is PATH-TRIGGERED: a PR touching only lib/src core never pays
  # for it (AC1), a lib/apps + js_ext diff does, and a classifier failure
  # fails safe (the leg runs). Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it —
  # gh-1538 retired the nightly flutter-app-macos full-suite backstop
  # (nightly is builds + integration-only now), so this pre-merge leg is
  # the macOS coverage for the JS-engine surface.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-exzone:
    name: Exclusion zone (macOS JS-engine tests)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true' &&
      needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 25
