With the PR's change, `run()` calls `kBootWatchdog.install()` which schedules `addPostFrameCallback` and arms a real 4s `Timer`. In a plain `test()` (not `testWidgets`), a real Timer of 4 seconds may fire if the test takes >4s... and `firstFrame()` would be called only when a frame lands — in a non-widget test no frame ever lands. The watchdog timer would fire at 4s and log a breadcrumb ("first frame not reached..."). Then re-arm every 30s up to 10 firings. That's harmless for the test itself unless the test framework complains about pending timers at the end of a `testWidgets` body... but these are plain `test()` bodies.

Hmm, but wait — `runWithEnv` test: `install()` called → `addPostFrameCallback` on TestWidgetsFlutterBinding. With FakeAsync? Plain `test()` in flutter_test runs in a normal zone. steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Pinned release must carry signed provenance
        run: bash scripts/check_install_pin.sh

  quality-gate:
    name: Quality gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, flutter-analyze, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, usage-fold, cli-visual-settings, cube-kernel-live, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env, fa-aot-build, pty-integration-linux, pty-coverage-gate, pty-visual, supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-verify, install-pin-gate, flutter-app-exzone, flutter-app-lock-smoke]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # #1368: the publish job consumes dart_ok — the pure-Dart package verdict
    # — instead of this aggregate's result. The aggregate itself stays the
    # single required check: any red leg (platform included) still fails it.
    outputs:
      dart_ok: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.dart_ok }}
    steps:
      - name: Report leg results
        run: |
          echo "static        = ${{ needs.static.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "test-core     = ${{ needs.test-core.result }}"
          echo "coverage-gate = ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "guards        = ${{ needs.guards.result }}"
          echo "flutter-analyze = ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}"
          echo "flutter-tests = ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}"
          echo "test-faui     = ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}"
          echo "app-crap-gate = ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}"
          echo "perf-gate     = ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}"
          echo "usage-fold    = ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}"
          echo "cube-live     = ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}"
          echo "cli-visual    = ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}"
          echo "build-web     = ${{ needs.build-web.result }}"
          echo "build-android = ${{ needs.build-android.result }}"
          echo "build-ios     = ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}"
          echo "build-macos   = ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}"
          echo "integ-mock    = ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "pty-integ-linux = ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}"
          echo "fa-aot-build  = ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}"
          echo "pty-gates     = ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "pty-visual    = ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}"
          echo "supply-chain  = ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}"
          echo "dep-audit     = ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}"
          echo "installer-it = ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}"
          echo "pin-gate    = ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}"
          echo "exzone      = ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}"
          echo "lock-smoke  = ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}"
      - name: Fail on any real failure (skipped security = dodge = FAIL)
        id: gate
        env:
          R_CHANGES: ${{ needs.changes.result }}
          R_SUPPLY_CHAIN: ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}
          R_DEP_AUDIT: ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}
          R_STATIC: ${{ needs.static.result }}
          R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE: ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}
          R_TEST_CORE: ${{ needs.test-core.result }}
          R_COVERAGE: ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}
          R_GUARDS: ${{ needs.guards.result }}
          R_FLUTTER: ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}
          R_CRAP: ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}
          R_FAUI: ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}
          R_PERF: ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}
          R_USAGE_FOLD: ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}
          R_CUBE: ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}
          R_CLI_VISUAL: ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}
          R_BUILD_WEB: ${{ needs.build-web.result }}
          R_BUILD_ANDROID: ${{ needs.build-android.result }}
          R_BUILD_IOS: ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}
          R_BUILD_MACOS: ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}
          R_INTEG: ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}
          R_HOSTILE: ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}
          R_PTY_LINUX: ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}
          R_FA_AOT: ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}
          R_PTY_GATES: ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}
          R_PTY_VISUAL: ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}
          R_INSTALLER_VERIFY: ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}
          R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE: ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}
          R_EXZONE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}
          R_LOCK_SMOKE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}
        run: |
          fail() { echo "Quality gate FAILED: $1"; exit 1; }
          # Verdict pass collects blockers WITHOUT exiting, so dart_ok is
          # always exported explicitly ('true' or 'false', never '') —
          # publish and the Provider smoke read this output and an empty
          # value must never read as either (review thread on #1370).
          dart_blocker=""
          # The classifier itself must have run: a failed or skipped
          # classifier skips EVERY downstream leg and would wave a PR
          # through with zero gates executed.
          [ "$R_CHANGES" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="changes classifier = $R_CHANGES"
          # Security legs must EXECUTE and pass. For these, skipped is a
          # dodge (e.g. a cunning diff that makes the classifier misfire),
          # not a pass — review follow-up, #796/#801.
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_SUPPLY_CHAIN" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="supply-chain = $R_SUPPLY_CHAIN (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_DEP_AUDIT" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="dep-audit = $R_DEP_AUDIT (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          # #1368 — two independent verdicts over the needs legs:
          #   PACKAGE legs (everything NOT platform) → dart_blocker: they
          #     gate dart_ok AND the aggregate — analyze/test/coverage must
          #     gate the publish (review thread: the case bodies were
          #     swapped in the first cut, re-enshrining the starvation);
          #   PLATFORM/NATIVE/PTY legs (build-web/android/ios/macos,
          #     fa-aot-build, installer-verify, install-pin-gate,
          #     cube-kernel-live, cli-visual-settings, pty-*) → platform_red
          #     only: they redden the required aggregate but NEVER dart_ok —
          #     a red Windows build must not hold the pure-Dart publish
          #     hostage (the v1.0.519-521 starvation).
          platform_red=false
          for kv in "static:$R_STATIC" "flutter-analyze:$R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE" "test-core:$R_TEST_CORE" "coverage-gate:$R_COVERAGE" \
                    "guards:$R_GUARDS" "flutter-tests:$R_FLUTTER" "app-crap-gate:$R_CRAP" \
                    "test-faui:$R_FAUI" "perf-gate:$R_PERF" "usage-fold:$R_USAGE_FOLD" "cube-kernel-live:$R_CUBE" \
                    "cli-visual-settings:$R_CLI_VISUAL" "build-web:$R_BUILD_WEB" \
                    "build-android:$R_BUILD_ANDROID" "build-ios:$R_BUILD_IOS" "build-macos:$R_BUILD_MACOS" \
                    "integration-mock:$R_INTEG" "hostile-env:$R_HOSTILE" \
                    "fa-aot-build:$R_FA_AOT" \
                    "pty-integration-linux:$R_PTY_LINUX" "pty-coverage-gate:$R_PTY_GATES" "pty-visual:$R_PTY_VISUAL" \
                    "installer-verify:$R_INSTALLER_VERIFY" "install-pin-gate:$R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE" \
                    "flutter-app-exzone:$R_EXZONE" "flutter-app-lock-smoke:$R_LOCK_SMOKE"; do

blocks.text:
flutter-tests:
    name: Flutter app tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    # End-of-run drain can stall minutes under shared-runner load while
    # every test already passed (0 failures, killed mid-drain on #330):
    # fa_ui shards get 12m and flutter_app is the heaviest package.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Bootstrap via git
      # clone instead: flutter_tools pulls the official arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # See flutter-analyze: placeholder must exist before pub get.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Golden suite is intentionally NOT here: goldens are host-locked
      # (same macOS host renders them differently across minor SDKs — see the
      # dynamic_messages saga) and would all redden on ubuntu. Widget/unit
      # tests run here on a cheap runner; goldens stay guarded by
      # build-macos.yml and the nightly full matrix (issue #177 E5/OQ3:
      # pinned-font golden migration is a follow-up, not this card).
      - name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
        # Goldens stay out (host-locked, see the golden comment above).
        # Native-dependent tests (quickjs_c_bridge .so, mic channel) are NOT
        # excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in
        # flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart + the injected-ASR fix.
        # Deterministic modulo split of the sorted file list: shard i takes
        # lines where NR % 2 == i — union == the old single job's list.
        run: |
          cd flutter_app
          find test -name '*_test.dart' ! -path '*/golden/*' ! -path '*/cli_visual/*' \
            | sort | awk -v i=${{ matrix.shard }} 'NR % 2 == i' > shard-files.txt
          echo "shard files: $(wc -l < shard-files.txt)"
          # --coverage (issue #433): each shard emits lcov for the
          # app-crap-gate job; the covered surface matches the CRAP
          # sources [lib] exactly.
          flutter test --exclude-tags integration --coverage $(cat shard-files.txt)

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: app-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

      # Issue #239 AC3: the App Store submission pre-flight matrix is plain
      # ruby over flutter_app/fastlane/appstore_preflight.rb — no gems,
      # runs in under a second on the runner's stock ruby.
      # Issue #289 adds the fastlane guard/preflight suites (android id
      # guard + Play upload pre-flight) — same plain-ruby contract, so the
      # step loops over every fastlane test file. Shard 0 only: once is
      # enough (fa PR #333).
      - name: Fastlane pre-flight suites (ruby)
        if: matrix.shard == 0
        run: |
          for t in flutter_app/fastlane/test/*_test.rb; do
            echo "::group::ruby $t"
            ruby "$t"
            echo "::endgroup::"
          done

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #1267 N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg. By #177 design the ubuntu
  # PR leg never EXERCISES the JS-engine suites: flutter_app/test/apps/**
  # skip their engine-dependent tests on ubuntu (native_test_guard.dart
  # finds no QuickJS .so on a bare runner), so that surface ran only in the
  # nightly macOS leg — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an
  # apps/engine regression merged green and went red the same night).
  #
  # Trigger model (issue #1267 N1 slice 2): ci.yml has NO pull_request
  # trigger — PR validation arrives as an SM workflow_dispatch on the head
  # SHA (machine-sm.yml). The changes classifier derives the validated diff
  # under BOTH events (merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) on dispatches), so
  # this leg is PATH-TRIGGERED: a PR touching only lib/src core never pays
  # for it (AC1), a lib/apps + js_ext diff does, and a classifier failure
  # fails safe (the leg runs). Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it —
  # gh-1538 retired the nightly flutter-app-macos full-suite backstop
  # (nightly is builds + integration-only now), so this pre-merge leg is
  # the macOS coverage for the JS-engine surface.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-exzone:
    name: Exclusion zone (macOS JS-engine tests)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true' &&
      needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 25

blocks.text:
The app_boot_test.dart exercises `FaAppBoot.run()` with `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized()`. With the PR's change, `run()` calls `kBootWatchdog.install()` which schedules `addPostFrameCallback` and arms a real 4s `Timer`. In a plain `test()` (not `testWidgets`), a real Timer of 4 seconds may fire if the test takes >4s... and `firstFrame()` would be called only when a frame lands — in a non-widget test no frame ever lands. The watchdog timer would fire at 4s and log a breadcrumb ("first frame not reached..."). Then re-arm every 30s up to 10 firings. That's harmless for the test itself unless the test framework complains about pending timers at the end of a `testWidgets` body... but these are plain `test()` bodies.

Hmm, but wait — `runWithEnv` test: `install()` called → `addPostFrameCallback` on TestWidgetsFlutterBinding. With FakeAsync? Plain `test()` in flutter_test runs in a normal zone. A pending Timer at the end of a plain test is NOT an error (unlike testWidgets which fails with "A Timer is still pending"). So that shouldn't fail.

Let me now check the progress of the background shards and, meanwhile, think about what else could be red.

Actually — hold on. Let me reconsider the failing checks:
- "Flutter app tests (shard 1/2)" — failure
- "Flutter app tests (shard 0/2)" — failure
- "Quality gate" — failure (aggregate)

Both shards red. If it were the boot watchdog tests, they'd all be in one shard (same directory, sorted adjacent → same shard). Something failing in BOTH shards = either (a) compile error affecting many tests, or (b) a widespread infra failure (e.g. pub get failure, firebase_options template missing, .env placeholder missing), or (c) two different genuine failures.

Since analyze passes locally with pub get done, and CI does the same steps... Actually wait — does CI's `flutter-analyze` leg also run on this head? It's in the needs list of quality-gate; only 3 checks failed: quality-gate, flutter-tests 0/2, 1/2. flutter-analyze must have passed (otherwise it'd be listed too). So code compiles. Runtime failures in both shards then.

Interesting: could this be the "timeout-minutes: 20" being hit? "End-of-run drain can stall minutes under shared-runner load" — timeout would mark the job failed without specific test failures. Both shards timing out (20 min) is plausible under heavy load — the previous CI comment says shard ~6 min though.

Or maybe the coverage upload step, or the fastlane step (shard 0 only)... but shard 1 also failed.

The arm64 runner (ubuntu-24.04-arm): "Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)" clones flutter stable. If the clone or precache failed (network flake), the job fails early. That could redden both shards as infra flake.

I genuinely need the CI logs. gh is rate-limited. Options: retry gh with a different token? The DMTools github tools might work — but there's no log-fetch tool. Hmm.

blocks.text:
flutter-tests:
    name: Flutter app tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    # End-of-run drain can stall minutes under shared-runner load while
    # every test already passed (0 failures, killed mid-drain on #330):
    # fa_ui shards get 12m and flutter_app is the heaviest package.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Bootstrap via git
      # clone instead: flutter_tools pulls the official arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # See flutter-analyze: placeholder must exist before pub get.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Golden suite is intentionally NOT here: goldens are host-locked
      # (same macOS host renders them differently across minor SDKs — see the
      # dynamic_messages saga) and would all redden on ubuntu. Widget/unit
      # tests run here on a cheap runner; goldens stay guarded by
      # build-macos.yml and the nightly full matrix (issue #177 E5/OQ3:
      # pinned-font golden migration is a follow-up, not this card).
      - name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
        # Goldens stay out (host-locked, see the golden comment above).
        # Native-dependent tests (quickjs_c_bridge .so, mic channel) are NOT
        # excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in
        # flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart + the injected-ASR fix.
        # Deterministic modulo split of the sorted file list: shard i takes
        # lines where NR % 2 == i — union == the old single job's list.
        run: |
          cd flutter_app
          find test -name '*_test.dart' ! -path '*/golden/*' ! -path '*/cli_visual/*' \
            | sort | awk -v i=${{ matrix.shard }} 'NR % 2 == i' > shard-files.txt
          echo "shard files: $(wc -l < shard-files.txt)"
          # --coverage (issue #433): each shard emits lcov for the
          # app-crap-gate job; the covered surface matches the CRAP
          # sources [lib] exactly.
          flutter test --exclude-tags integration --coverage $(cat shard-files.txt)

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: app-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

      # Issue #239 AC3: the App Store submission pre-flight matrix is plain
      # ruby over flutter_app/fastlane/appstore_preflight.rb — no gems,
      # runs in under a second on the runner's stock ruby.
      # Issue #289 adds the fastlane guard/preflight suites (android id
      # guard + Play upload pre-flight) — same plain-ruby contract, so the
      # step loops over every fastlane test file. Shard 0 only: once is
      # enough (fa PR #333).
      - name: Fastlane pre-flight suites (ruby)
        if: matrix.shard == 0
        run: |
          for t in flutter_app/fastlane/test/*_test.rb; do
            echo "::group::ruby $t"
            ruby "$t"
            echo "::endgroup::"
          done

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #1267 N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg. By #177 design the ubuntu
  # PR leg never EXERCISES the JS-engine suites: flutter_app/test/apps/**
  # skip their engine-dependent tests on ubuntu (native_test_guard.dart
  # finds no QuickJS .so on a bare runner), so that surface ran only in the
  # nightly macOS leg — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an
  # apps/engine regression merged green and went red the same night).
  #
  # Trigger model (issue #1267 N1 slice 2): ci.yml has NO pull_request
  # trigger — PR validation arrives as an SM workflow_dispatch on the head
  # SHA (machine-sm.yml). The changes classifier derives the validated diff
  # under BOTH events (merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) on dispatches), so
  # this leg is PATH-TRIGGERED: a PR touching only lib/src core never pays
  # for it (AC1), a lib/apps + js_ext diff does, and a classifier failure
  # fails safe (the leg runs). Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it —
  # gh-1538 retired the nightly flutter-app-macos full-suite backstop
  # (nightly is builds + integration-only now), so this pre-merge leg is
  # the macOS coverage for the JS-engine surface.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-exzone:
    name: Exclusion zone (macOS JS-engine tests)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true' &&
      needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 25

blocks.text:
The app_boot_test.dart exercises `FaAppBoot.run()` with `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized()`. With the PR's change, `run()` calls `kBootWatchdog.install()` which schedules `addPostFrameCallback` and arms a real 4s `Timer`. In a plain `test()` (not `testWidgets`), a real Timer of 4 seconds may fire if the test takes >4s... and `firstFrame()` would be called only when a frame lands — in a non-widget test no frame ever lands. The watchdog timer would fire at 4s and log a breadcrumb ("first frame not reached..."). Then re-arm every 30s up to 10 firings. That's harmless for the test itself unless the test framework complains about pending timers at the end of a `testWidgets` body... but these are plain `test()` bodies.

Hmm, but wait — `runWithEnv` test: `install()` called → `addPostFrameCallback` on TestWidgetsFlutterBinding. With FakeAsync? Plain `test()` in flutter_test runs in a normal zone. A pending Timer at the end of a plain test is NOT an error (unlike testWidgets which fails with "A Timer is still pending"). So that shouldn't fail.

Let me now check the progress of the background shards and, meanwhile, think about what else could be red.

Actually — hold on. Let me reconsider the failing checks:
- "Flutter app tests (shard 1/2)" — failure
- "Flutter app tests (shard 0/2)" — failure
- "Quality gate" — failure (aggregate)

Both shards red. If it were the boot watchdog tests, they'd all be in one shard (same directory, sorted adjacent → same shard). Something failing in BOTH shards = either (a) compile error affecting many tests, or (b) a widespread infra failure (e.g. pub get failure, firebase_options template missing, .env placeholder missing), or (c) two different genuine failures.

Since analyze passes locally with pub get done, and CI does the same steps... Actually wait — does CI's `flutter-analyze` leg also run on this head? It's in the needs list of quality-gate; only 3 checks failed: quality-gate, flutter-tests 0/2, 1/2. flutter-analyze must have passed (otherwise it'd be listed too). So code compiles. Runtime failures in both shards then.

Interesting: could this be the "timeout-minutes: 20" being hit? "End-of-run drain can stall minutes under shared-runner load" — timeout would mark the job failed without specific test failures. Both shards timing out (20 min) is plausible under heavy load — the previous CI comment says shard ~6 min though.

Or maybe the coverage upload step, or the fastlane step (shard 0 only)... but shard 1 also failed.

The arm64 runner (ubuntu-24.04-arm): "Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)" clones flutter stable. If the clone or precache failed (network flake), the job fails early. That could redden both shards as infra flake.

I genuinely need the CI logs. gh is rate-limited. Options: retry gh with a different token? The DMTools github tools might work — but there's no log-fetch tool. Hmm.

messages.preview: The pending timer is the **restore-phase 10s Timer** from `beginRestore()` — armed in `_boot()` but never disarmed by the time the test ends. Let me collect all failing tests in both shards.

blocks.text:
The failure is confirmed:

**Shard 0**: `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` — "first boot: onboarding → skip → setup → connect → launcher home" — `A Timer is still pending even after the widget tree was disposed` — the pending timer is the **restore-phase 10s Timer** created by `BootWatchdog.beginRestore()` (called from `_BootstrapScreenState._boot` at main.dart:666) — because the restore never completed before the test ended (or completed but... no wait, `restoreDone()` in `finally` cancels the timer. Let me think).

Stack trace: the pending timer was created at `BootWatchdog._arm` ← `beginRestore` ← `_BootstrapScreenState._boot` (main.dart:666). So `beginRestore()` armed a 10s restore timer. For the test to end with the timer pending, `restoreDone()` must NOT have run — i.e., the restore chain did not complete (or the test finished before the async chain reached the `finally`).

Hmm wait — in the boot_flows test, "first boot: onboarding → skip → setup → connect → launcher home" — the flow taps through onboarding, setup, connect, and reaches launcher home. The `_boot()` chain: `beginRestore()` → createPlatformEnv → FlutterSessionManager → `createOrResumeSession` → ... → navigate to home → finally `restoreDone()`. The test reaches launcher home, meaning `onHome` ran... but did `createOrResumeSession` complete? The navigation happens inside the same `_boot()` future after the restore completes... Actually looking at main.dart's `_boot()`: after `BootSteps.mark('restore:session')`, it navigates. So by the time launcher home is reached, `createOrResumeSession` completed, and then the `finally` runs `restoreDone()`. Unless the test finished pumping before the `finally` microtask ran — the pending timer was created during the tap handling (stack: `_OnboardingScreenState._finish` → `_onboardingFinished` → `_boot` → `beginRestore`).

The test asserts pending timers at the END of the test body. If `_boot()` completes fully (restore done), the timer gets cancelled in the `finally`... but only if the whole `_boot()` future runs to completion within the test. In a `testWidgets`, all this runs on fake async; after the test body completes, the binding drains microtasks but real async chains that are waiting on real I/O (platform channels) may stall... In the test environment, `createPlatformEnv` and `createOrResumeSession` do run via test harness fakes (the test drives a full boot flow).

The failure says the 10s restore Timer is STILL pending at test end. That means `restoreDone()` never executed — the `_boot()` chain hadn't finished when the test body ended. Actually more precisely: it means the future created by `_boot()` (fired from the tap) hadn't completed. blocks.text:
flutter-tests:
    name: Flutter app tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    # End-of-run drain can stall minutes under shared-runner load while
    # every test already passed (0 failures, killed mid-drain on #330):
    # fa_ui shards get 12m and flutter_app is the heaviest package.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Bootstrap via git
      # clone instead: flutter_tools pulls the official arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # See flutter-analyze: placeholder must exist before pub get.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Golden suite is intentionally NOT here: goldens are host-locked
      # (same macOS host renders them differently across minor SDKs — see the
      # dynamic_messages saga) and would all redden on ubuntu. Widget/unit
      # tests run here on a cheap runner; goldens stay guarded by
      # build-macos.yml and the nightly full matrix (issue #177 E5/OQ3:
      # pinned-font golden migration is a follow-up, not this card).
      - name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
        # Goldens stay out (host-locked, see the golden comment above).
        # Native-dependent tests (quickjs_c_bridge .so, mic channel) are NOT
        # excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in
        # flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart + the injected-ASR fix.
        # Deterministic modulo split of the sorted file list: shard i takes
        # lines where NR % 2 == i — union == the old single job's list.
        run: |
          cd flutter_app
          find test -name '*_test.dart' ! -path '*/golden/*' ! -path '*/cli_visual/*' \
            | sort | awk -v i=${{ matrix.shard }} 'NR % 2 == i' > shard-files.txt
          echo "shard files: $(wc -l < shard-files.txt)"
          # --coverage (issue #433): each shard emits lcov for the
          # app-crap-gate job; the covered surface matches the CRAP
          # sources [lib] exactly.
          flutter test --exclude-tags integration --coverage $(cat shard-files.txt)

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: app-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

      # Issue #239 AC3: the App Store submission pre-flight matrix is plain
      # ruby over flutter_app/fastlane/appstore_preflight.rb — no gems,
      # runs in under a second on the runner's stock ruby.
      # Issue #289 adds the fastlane guard/preflight suites (android id
      # guard + Play upload pre-flight) — same plain-ruby contract, so the
      # step loops over every fastlane test file. Shard 0 only: once is
      # enough (fa PR #333).
      - name: Fastlane pre-flight suites (ruby)
        if: matrix.shard == 0
        run: |
          for t in flutter_app/fastlane/test/*_test.rb; do
            echo "::group::ruby $t"
            ruby "$t"
            echo "::endgroup::"
          done

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #1267 N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg. By #177 design the ubuntu
  # PR leg never EXERCISES the JS-engine suites: flutter_app/test/apps/**
  # skip their engine-dependent tests on ubuntu (native_test_guard.dart
  # finds no QuickJS .so on a bare runner), so that surface ran only in the
  # nightly macOS leg — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an
  # apps/engine regression merged green and went red the same night).
  #
  # Trigger model (issue #1267 N1 slice 2): ci.yml has NO pull_request
  # trigger — PR validation arrives as an SM workflow_dispatch on the head
  # SHA (machine-sm.yml). The changes classifier derives the validated diff
  # under BOTH events (merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) on dispatches), so
  # this leg is PATH-TRIGGERED: a PR touching only lib/src core never pays
  # for it (AC1), a lib/apps + js_ext diff does, and a classifier failure
  # fails safe (the leg runs). Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it —
  # gh-1538 retired the nightly flutter-app-macos full-suite backstop
  # (nightly is builds + integration-only now), so this pre-merge leg is
  # the macOS coverage for the JS-engine surface.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-exzone:
    name: Exclusion zone (macOS JS-engine tests)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true' &&
      needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 25

content.thinking:
Confirmed root cause. Both failing tests are the same pattern:

1. **shard 0**: `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` — "first boot: onboarding → skip → setup → connect → launcher home" — pending 10s restore Timer created by `beginRestore()` from `_boot()` (via `_onboardingFinished`).
2. **shard 1**: `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` — "a restorable connection boots straight to the spinner" — pending 10s restore Timer created by `beginRestore()` from `_boot()` (via `initState` post-frame).

Both fail with "A Timer is still pending even after the widget tree was disposed" (`!timersPending`).

Why is the timer still pending? In both cases, `_boot()`'s restore chain is in flight when the test body completes:
- Test 2 ("boots straight to the spinner"): the test pumps the BootstrapScreen, the post-frame `_boot()` starts the restore (arms the 10s timer), and the test asserts the spinner is showing — the restore is INTENTIONALLY still in flight when the test ends. `restoreDone()` never runs because the restore hasn't completed. The 10s timer remains pending → invariant violation.
- Test 1 (boot_flows first boot): taps through onboarding → setup → connect → launcher home. `_onboardingFinished` → `_boot()` arms the restore timer; the test reaches launcher home... but the pending timer suggests the `_boot()` future never completed within the test's fake-async lifetime. Possibly the restore chain is stuck awaiting something (the test environment stalls it — e.g. an agent service awaiting network that never completes under the test binding), or the test ends before the chain drains. Either way, the timer is still armed at test end.

Now — the fix. Options:

**Option A: Make the watchdog test-aware.** In test environments (`Platform.environment.containsKey('FLUTTER_TEST')`), skip arming or use zero durations. But the pending-timer invariant would still trip if we arm timers in testWidgets... Well, if we don't arm at all under FLUTTER_TEST, no timers, tests pass. But then the boot tests wouldn't exercise the watchdog — that's what the dedicated boot_watchdog_test.dart with fakeAsync is for. This is a common pattern (CI-only guards exist elsewhere in this repo: `native_test_guard.dart` etc.).

**Option B: In `_boot()`, disarm more aggressively** — restoreDone() in finally already runs when the chain completes; the problem is tests that END while the chain is in flight. Can't fix from production code — the test ends mid-flight by design ("boots straight to the spinner").

**Option C: Use `Timer` with `FakeAsync`-friendly API**... no such thing.

The right fix per repo conventions: check how other boot-path timers handle this. E.g. "skill seeding 5 s timeout", "180 s provider connect watchdog" — how do they avoid pending-timer failures in widget tests? Let me look at existing patterns, e.g. the provider connect watchdog or skill seeding timeout.

Let me search for how existing timers in the boot path are gated for tests.

blocks.text:
flutter-tests:
    name: Flutter app tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    # End-of-run drain can stall minutes under shared-runner load while
    # every test already passed (0 failures, killed mid-drain on #330):
    # fa_ui shards get 12m and flutter_app is the heaviest package.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Bootstrap via git
      # clone instead: flutter_tools pulls the official arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # See flutter-analyze: placeholder must exist before pub get.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Golden suite is intentionally NOT here: goldens are host-locked
      # (same macOS host renders them differently across minor SDKs — see the
      # dynamic_messages saga) and would all redden on ubuntu. Widget/unit
      # tests run here on a cheap runner; goldens stay guarded by
      # build-macos.yml and the nightly full matrix (issue #177 E5/OQ3:
      # pinned-font golden migration is a follow-up, not this card).
      - name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
        # Goldens stay out (host-locked, see the golden comment above).
        # Native-dependent tests (quickjs_c_bridge .so, mic channel) are NOT
        # excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in
        # flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart + the injected-ASR fix.
        # Deterministic modulo split of the sorted file list: shard i takes
        # lines where NR % 2 == i — union == the old single job's list.
        run: |
          cd flutter_app
          find test -name '*_test.dart' ! -path '*/golden/*' ! -path '*/cli_visual/*' \
            | sort | awk -v i=${{ matrix.shard }} 'NR % 2 == i' > shard-files.txt
          echo "shard files: $(wc -l < shard-files.txt)"
          # --coverage (issue #433): each shard emits lcov for the
          # app-crap-gate job; the covered surface matches the CRAP
          # sources [lib] exactly.
          flutter test --exclude-tags integration --coverage $(cat shard-files.txt)

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: app-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

      # Issue #239 AC3: the App Store submission pre-flight matrix is plain
      # ruby over flutter_app/fastlane/appstore_preflight.rb — no gems,
      # runs in under a second on the runner's stock ruby.
      # Issue #289 adds the fastlane guard/preflight suites (android id
      # guard + Play upload pre-flight) — same plain-ruby contract, so the
      # step loops over every fastlane test file. Shard 0 only: once is
      # enough (fa PR #333).
      - name: Fastlane pre-flight suites (ruby)
        if: matrix.shard == 0
        run: |
          for t in flutter_app/fastlane/test/*_test.rb; do
            echo "::group::ruby $t"
            ruby "$t"
            echo "::endgroup::"
          done

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #1267 N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg. By #177 design the ubuntu
  # PR leg never EXERCISES the JS-engine suites: flutter_app/test/apps/**
  # skip their engine-dependent tests on ubuntu (native_test_guard.dart
  # finds no QuickJS .so on a bare runner), so that surface ran only in the
  # nightly macOS leg — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an
  # apps/engine regression merged green and went red the same night).
  #
  # Trigger model (issue #1267 N1 slice 2): ci.yml has NO pull_request
  # trigger — PR validation arrives as an SM workflow_dispatch on the head
  # SHA (machine-sm.yml). The changes classifier derives the validated diff
  # under BOTH events (merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) on dispatches), so
  # this leg is PATH-TRIGGERED: a PR touching only lib/src core never pays
  # for it (AC1), a lib/apps + js_ext diff does, and a classifier failure
  # fails safe (the leg runs). Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it —
  # gh-1538 retired the nightly flutter-app-macos full-suite backstop
  # (nightly is builds + integration-only now), so this pre-merge leg is
  # the macOS coverage for the JS-engine surface.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-exzone:
    name: Exclusion zone (macOS JS-engine tests)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true' &&
      needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 25

For the test to end with the timer pending, `restoreDone()` must NOT have run — i.e., the restore chain did not complete (or the test finished before the async chain reached the `finally`).

Hmm wait — in the boot_flows test, "first boot: onboarding → skip → setup → connect → launcher home" — the flow taps through onboarding, setup, connect, and reaches launcher home. The `_boot()` chain: `beginRestore()` → createPlatformEnv → FlutterSessionManager → `createOrResumeSession` → ... → navigate to home → finally `restoreDone()`. The test reaches launcher home, meaning `onHome` ran... but did `createOrResumeSession` complete? The navigation happens inside the same `_boot()` future after the restore completes... Actually looking at main.dart's `_boot()`: after `BootSteps.mark('restore:session')`, it navigates. So by the time launcher home is reached, `createOrResumeSession` completed, and then the `finally` runs `restoreDone()`. Unless the test finished pumping before the `finally` microtask ran — the pending timer was created during the tap handling (stack: `_OnboardingScreenState._finish` → `_onboardingFinished` → `_boot` → `beginRestore`).

The test asserts pending timers at the END of the test body. If `_boot()` completes fully (restore done), the timer gets cancelled in the `finally`... but only if the whole `_boot()` future runs to completion within the test. In a `testWidgets`, all this runs on fake async; after the test body completes, the binding drains microtasks but real async chains that are waiting on real I/O (platform channels) may stall... In the test environment, `createPlatformEnv` and `createOrResumeSession` do run via test harness fakes (the test drives a full boot flow).

The failure says the 10s restore Timer is STILL pending at test end. That means `restoreDone()` never executed — the `_boot()` chain hadn't finished when the test body ended. Actually more precisely: it means the future created by `_boot()` (fired from the tap) hadn't completed. The test taps through the UI and ends; the boot chain may be mid-flight (e.g., awaiting something the test didn't pump through, like `pumpAndSettle` timing out or the test just not pumping long enough).

Regardless of the exact stall point, the design issue: **the watchdog arms real Timers during widget-test-driven boot flows and the tests end with them pending**. The pre-frame 4s timer didn't show up as pending because `firstFrame()` cancels it when a frame lands (testWidgets pumps frames). But the restore 10s timer stays armed whenever a `_boot()` restore is still in flight (or its `finally` hasn't run) when the test body ends.

Wait — but actually if the restore completed, `restoreDone` cancels. The boot_flows test does reach launcher home... Let me look at the boot_flows_test to understand what's happening. Confirmed root cause. Both failing tests are the same pattern:

1. **shard 0**: `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` — "first boot: onboarding → skip → setup → connect → launcher home" — pending 10s restore Timer created by `beginRestore()` from `_boot()` (via `_onboardingFinished`).
2. **shard 1**: `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` — "a restorable connection boots straight to the spinner" — pending 10s restore Timer created by `beginRestore()` from `_boot()` (via `initState` post-frame).

Both fail with "A Timer is still pending even after the widget tree was disposed" (`!timersPending`).

Why is the timer still pending? In both cases, `_boot()`'s restore chain is in flight when the test body completes:
- Test 2 ("boots straight to the spinner"): the test pumps the BootstrapScreen, the post-frame `_boot()` starts the restore (arms the 10s timer), and the test asserts the spinner is showing — the restore is INTENTIONALLY still in flight when the test ends. `restoreDone()` never runs because the restore hasn't completed. The 10s timer remains pending → invariant violation.
- Test 1 (boot_flows first boot): taps through onboarding → setup → connect → launcher home. `_onboardingFinished` → `_boot()` arms the restore timer; the test reaches launcher home... but the pending timer suggests the `_boot()` future never completed within the test's fake-async lifetime. Possibly the restore chain is stuck awaiting something (the test environment stalls it — e.g. an agent service awaiting network that never completes under the test binding), or the test ends before the chain drains. Either way, the timer is still armed at test end.

Now — the fix. Options:

**Option A: Make the watchdog test-aware.** In test environments (`Platform.environment.containsKey('FLUTTER_TEST')`), skip arming or use zero durations. But the pending-timer invariant would still trip if we arm timers in testWidgets... Well, if we don't arm at all under FLUTTER_TEST, no timers, tests pass. But then the boot tests wouldn't exercise the watchdog — that's what the dedicated boot_watchdog_test.dart with fakeAsync is for. This is a common pattern (CI-only guards exist elsewhere in this repo: `native_test_guard.dart` etc.).

**Option B: In `_boot()`, disarm more aggressively** — restoreDone() in finally already runs when the chain completes; the problem is tests that END while the chain is in flight. Can't fix from production code — the test ends mid-flight by design ("boots straight to the spinner").

**Option C: Use `Timer` with `FakeAsync`-friendly API**... no such thing.

The right fix per repo conventions: check how other boot-path timers handle this. E.g. "skill seeding 5 s timeout", "180 s provider connect watchdog" — how do they avoid pending-timer failures in widget tests? Let me look at existing patterns, e.g. the provider connect watchdog or skill seeding timeout.

flutter-tests:
    name: Flutter app tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    # End-of-run drain can stall minutes under shared-runner load while
    # every test already passed (0 failures, killed mid-drain on #330):
    # fa_ui shards get 12m and flutter_app is the heaviest package.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Bootstrap via git
      # clone instead: flutter_tools pulls the official arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # See flutter-analyze: placeholder must exist before pub get.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Golden suite is intentionally NOT here: goldens are host-locked
      # (same macOS host renders them differently across minor SDKs — see the
      # dynamic_messages saga) and would all redden on ubuntu. Widget/unit
      # tests run here on a cheap runner; goldens stay guarded by
      # build-macos.yml and the nightly full matrix (issue #177 E5/OQ3:
      # pinned-font golden migration is a follow-up, not this card).
      - name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
        # Goldens stay out (host-locked, see the golden comment above).
        # Native-dependent tests (quickjs_c_bridge .so, mic channel) are NOT
        # excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in
        # flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart + the injected-ASR fix.
        # Deterministic modulo split of the sorted file list: shard i takes
        # lines where NR % 2 == i — union == the old single job's list.
        run: |
          cd flutter_app
          find test -name '*_test.dart' ! -path '*/golden/*' ! -path '*/cli_visual/*' \
            | sort | awk -v i=${{ matrix.shard }} 'NR % 2 == i' > shard-files.txt
          echo "shard files: $(wc -l < shard-files.txt)"
          # --coverage (issue #433): each shard emits lcov for the
          # app-crap-gate job; the covered surface matches the CRAP
          # sources [lib] exactly.
          flutter test --exclude-tags integration --coverage $(cat shard-files.txt)

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: app-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

      # Issue #239 AC3: the App Store submission pre-flight matrix is plain
      # ruby over flutter_app/fastlane/appstore_preflight.rb — no gems,
      # runs in under a second on the runner's stock ruby.
      # Issue #289 adds the fastlane guard/preflight suites (android id
      # guard + Play upload pre-flight) — same plain-ruby contract, so the
      # step loops over every fastlane test file. Shard 0 only: once is
      # enough (fa PR #333).
      - name: Fastlane pre-flight suites (ruby)
        if: matrix.shard == 0
        run: |
          for t in flutter_app/fastlane/test/*_test.rb; do
            echo "::group::ruby $t"
            ruby "$t"
            echo "::endgroup::"
          done

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #1267 N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg. By #177 design the ubuntu
  # PR leg never EXERCISES the JS-engine suites: flutter_app/test/apps/**
  # skip their engine-dependent tests on ubuntu (native_test_guard.dart
  # finds no QuickJS .so on a bare runner), so that surface ran only in the
  # nightly macOS leg — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an
  # apps/engine regression merged green and went red the same night).
  #
  # Trigger model (issue #1267 N1 slice 2): ci.yml has NO pull_request
  # trigger — PR validation arrives as an SM workflow_dispatch on the head
  # SHA (machine-sm.yml). The changes classifier derives the validated diff
  # under BOTH events (merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) on dispatches), so
  # this leg is PATH-TRIGGERED: a PR touching only lib/src core never pays
  # for it (AC1), a lib/apps + js_ext diff does, and a classifier failure
  # fails safe (the leg runs). Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it —

Confirmed root cause. Both failing tests are the same pattern:

1. **shard 0**: `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` — "first boot: onboarding → skip → setup → connect → launcher home" — pending 10s restore Timer created by `beginRestore()` from `_boot()` (via `_onboardingFinished`).
2. **shard 1**: `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` — "a restorable connection boots straight to the spinner" — pending 10s restore Timer created by `beginRestore()` from `_boot()` (via `initState` post-frame).

Both fail with "A Timer is still pending even after the widget tree was disposed" (`!timersPending`).

Why is the timer still pending? In both cases, `_boot()`'s restore chain is in flight when the test body completes:
- Test 2 ("boots straight to the spinner"): the test pumps the BootstrapScreen, the post-frame `_boot()` starts the restore (arms the 10s timer), and the test asserts the spinner is showing — the restore is INTENTIONALLY still in flight when the test ends. `restoreDone()` never runs because the restore hasn't completed. The 10s timer remains pending → invariant violation.
- Test 1 (boot_flows first boot): taps through onboarding → setup → connect → launcher home. `_onboardingFinished` → `_boot()` arms the restore timer; the test reaches launcher home... but the pending timer suggests the `_boot()` future never completed within the test's fake-async lifetime. Possibly the restore chain is stuck awaiting something (the test environment stalls it — e.g. an agent service awaiting network that never completes under the test binding), or the test ends before the chain drains. Either way, the timer is still armed at test end.

Now — the fix. Options:

**Option A: Make the watchdog test-aware.** In test environments (`Platform.environment.containsKey('FLUTTER_TEST')`), skip arming or use zero durations. But the pending-timer invariant would still trip if we arm timers in testWidgets... Well, if we don't arm at all under FLUTTER_TEST, no timers, tests pass. But then the boot tests wouldn't exercise the watchdog — that's what the dedicated boot_watchdog_test.dart with fakeAsync is for. This is a common pattern (CI-only guards exist elsewhere in this repo: `native_test_guard.dart` etc.).

**Option B: In `_boot()`, disarm more aggressively** — restoreDone() in finally already runs when the chain completes; the problem is tests that END while the chain is in flight. Can't fix from production code — the test ends mid-flight by design ("boots straight to the spinner").

**Option C: Use `Timer` with `FakeAsync`-friendly API**... no such thing.

Confirmed root cause. Both failing tests are the same pattern:

1. **shard 0**: `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` — "first boot: onboarding → skip → setup → connect → launcher home" — pending 10s restore Timer created by `beginRestore()` from `_boot()` (via `_onboardingFinished`).
2. **shard 1**: `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` — "a restorable connection boots straight to the spinner" — pending 10s restore Timer created by `beginRestore()` from `_boot()` (via `initState` post-frame).

blocks.text:
Confirmed root cause. Both failing tests are the same pattern:

1. **shard 0**: `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` — "first boot: onboarding → skip → setup → connect → launcher home" — pending 10s restore Timer created by `beginRestore()` from `_boot()` (via `_onboardingFinished`).
2. **shard 1**: `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` — "a restorable connection boots straight to the spinner" — pending 10s restore Timer created by `beginRestore()` from `_boot()` (via `initState` post-frame).

Both fail with "A Timer is still pending even after the widget tree was disposed" (`!timersPending`).

Why is the timer still pending? In both cases, `_boot()`'s restore chain is in flight when the test body completes:
- Test 2 ("boots straight to the spinner"): the test pumps the BootstrapScreen, the post-frame `_boot()` starts the restore (arms the 10s timer), and the test asserts the spinner is showing — the restore is INTENTIONALLY still in flight when the test ends. `restoreDone()` never runs because the restore hasn't completed. The 10s timer remains pending → invariant violation.
- Test 1 (boot_flows first boot): taps through onboarding → setup → connect → launcher home. `_onboardingFinished` → `_boot()` arms the restore timer; the test reaches launcher home... but the pending timer suggests the `_boot()` future never completed within the test's fake-async lifetime. Possibly the restore chain is stuck awaiting something (the test environment stalls it — e.g. an agent service awaiting network that never completes under the test binding), or the test ends before the chain drains. Either way, the timer is still armed at test end.

Now — the fix. Options:

**Option A: Make the watchdog test-aware.** In test environments (`Platform.environment.containsKey('FLUTTER_TEST')`), skip arming or use zero durations. But the pending-timer invariant would still trip if we arm timers in testWidgets... Well, if we don't arm at all under FLUTTER_TEST, no timers, tests pass. But then the boot tests wouldn't exercise the watchdog — that's what the dedicated boot_watchdog_test.dart with fakeAsync is for. This is a common pattern (CI-only guards exist elsewhere in this repo: `native_test_guard.dart` etc.).

**Option B: In `_boot()`, disarm more aggressively** — restoreDone() in finally already runs when the chain completes; the problem is tests that END while the chain is in flight. Can't fix from production code — the test ends mid-flight by design ("boots straight to the spinner").

**Option C: Use `Timer` with `FakeAsync`-friendly API**... no such thing.

The right fix per repo conventions: check how other boot-path timers handle this. E.g. "skill seeding 5 s timeout", "180 s provider connect watchdog" — how do they avoid pending-timer failures in widget tests? Let me look at existing patterns, e.g. the provider connect watchdog or skill seeding timeout.

The same exact rationale applies to the boot watchdog. The watchdog under `flutter test`:
- The pre-frame 4s Timer gets cancelled by `firstFrame()` in most widget tests (frames pump) — that's why only the 10s restore timer showed up as pending. But boot_flows_test also had failures... only ONE test in boot_flows failed though. Other boot_flows tests passed — meaning in most tests the restore chain completes (finally → restoreDone cancels), and in the two failing tests the chain is still in flight at test end (spinner test intentionally; first-boot test maybe awaiting something async that the test doesn't drive to completion).

Look at the trace again: the timer was created during the tap on the onboarding screen (`_finish` → `_onboardingFinished` → `_boot`). Actually — the `restoreDone()` cancel path: `if (!_restoreArmed) return;` — `beginRestore()` sets `_restoreArmed = true` and arms. `restoreDone()` sets false, cancels. That should work...

Unless `_boot()` future never completed because after navigation, something awaits forever (e.g. `navigator.pushReplacement(...)` — awaits the route's completion? `pushReplacement` completes when the new route is popped... no, pushReplacement returns a Future that completes when the pushed route is popped. Confirmed — **two bugs**:

**Bug 1 (the CI red):** `await navigator.pushReplacement(...)` inside `_boot()` — this future stays pending while the home screen is on top (it completes only when home is popped). So in a *successful* boot, `restoreDone()` (in `finally`) does NOT run until the user navigates away from home — effectively never. Consequences:
- Widget tests that boot to home (`boot_flows_test` first-boot, `onboarding_screen_test` spinner test) end with the restore 10s Timer still pending → `!timersPending` invariant → test failure. (The "skips onboarding" test passed — likely because in that test the widget tree got torn down such that `mounted` was false before navigation, letting `_boot` return early through the finally.)

Wait, let me double check the "skips onboarding" pass vs "boots straight to the spinner" fail. In the spinner test, the test asserts the spinner is showing (restore in flight, nav hasn't happened) — the timer pending at end is EXPECTED because restore is still in flight. In the first-boot test, home reached → pushReplacement pending → finally not run → timer pending.

**Bug 2 (production noise, same root):** In production, every successful boot leaves the restore watchdog armed while the user is on home → after 10s it fires "restore not completed after ..." breadcrumbs, repeating every 30s ×10, then "giving up". Every launch, ~11 spurious diagnostic lines + Crashlytics breadcrumb trail pollution, and it masks real wedges. The PR's own test `restoreDone inside the threshold is silent` doesn't catch this because it calls `restoreDone()` directly.

**The fix (surgical, addresses both):**

1. In `_boot()`: disarm the restore phase as soon as the restore itself is done — the watchdog's job is the restore chain, not the navigation. Move `restoreDone()` (or an explicit `BootSteps`-aware disarm) to right after the restore completes and before the navigation await. Specifically:
   - after `BootSteps.mark('restore:session')` and the mounted check... hmm, but the `finally` must still disarm on the failure path. Cleanest: call `restoreDone()` immediately after the restore chain completes (success), and keep `finally` for the failure path (restoreDone is idempotent — `if (!_restoreArmed) return;`).
   
   Actually simplest correct structure: since `restoreDone()` is idempotent, call it right after `createOrResumeSession` completes (mark restore:session), and keep the `finally` as a safety net for the catch path. On the catch path (restore failed), the finally disarms. On the success path, restoreDone runs early (before pushReplacement), so the timer is cancelled before navigation.

   Also `_bootRelay()` has the same shape: `beginRestore()` → `await bootExtensionRelay(...)` where `onHome` navigates... let me check bootExtensionRelay: does it await the navigation? In `bootExtensionRelay`, `onHome` is called and awaited? Looking at the earlier diff, `_bootRelay`'s `onHome` awaits `navigator.pushReplacement` too. If `bootExtensionRelay` awaits `onHome(...)`, then the same bug exists: finally runs only after home pops. Same fix needed: disarm after the relay restore completes but before/independent of the navigation... but in `_bootRelay` the navigation happens inside the `onHome` callback, so disarm after `bootExtensionRelay` returns won't help either (it awaits onHome → pushReplacement pending forever).

That's the established repo convention for exactly this failure mode ("real engine spawns periodic native-bridge timers that outlive the widget tree and trip the test binding's 'Timer still pending' invariant").

   With a test-binding guard in `BootWatchdog._arm` (no-op timers under `flutter test`):

The fake_async tests use `FakeAsync().run` with plain `test()` — does that install the binding? `test()` from flutter_test does NOT install TestWidgetsFlutterBinding (unless TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized is called). The boot_watchdog_test.dart uses plain `fakeAsync((async) {...})` — no binding → runtimeType check passes (binding not initialized... wait, `WidgetsBinding.instance` THROWS if binding not initialized!).

   In boot_watchdog_test.dart's `watchdogWith` helper — let me check if it initializes the binding. If the guard does `WidgetsBinding.instance.runtimeType` it would throw in those tests where the binding isn't initialized. I need a safe probe like app_boot_test's `_flutterBindingInitialized()` try/catch pattern.

   Alternatively gate on the default (production) constructor path only... cleaner: in `_arm()`, if a test binding is active → create the timer anyway? No — pending-timer invariant.

   Design: add a `timersEnabled` flag or make `_arm` skip arming when a test binding is present:

```dart
/// True under `flutter test` (same probe as app_tile_host): the test
/// binding fails ANY test that ends with timers still pending
/// (`!timersPending`), and boot flows legitimately end mid-restore

/// never arms real timers. Covered by the fake_async suite; production

static bool get _underTestBinding {
  try {
    return WidgetsBinding.instance.runtimeType
        .toString()
        .contains('TestWidgetsFlutterBinding');
  } on FlutterError {
    return false; // no binding (pure-Dart fake_async tests) → arm normally

And in `_arm`: `if (_underTestBinding) return;`

Hmm, but then in testWidgets-based boot flows, `firstFrame()` still runs (post-frame callback) — fine, it cancels nothing and logs only if firings > 0.

But wait — there's a wrinkle: the boot_watchdog_test.dart's existing tests run under `fake_async`'s FakeAsync WITHOUT a widgets binding? Let me check the test file — `watchdogWith(breadcrumbs)` helper. If the tests call `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized()` somewhere, the probe would return true and disable timers, breaking all 33 tests! Let me read the test file.

Also there's ANOTHER subtlety: `flutter test` compiles each test file separately; `test/boot_watchdog_test.dart` — if it uses plain `test()` + `fakeAsync`, no binding → probes false → timers arm (FakeAsync timers) → tests pass as before. 

And for widget tests (boot_flows etc.), timers won't arm → invariant holds → green.

Skipping under the test binding is a standard, documented pattern in this repo (app_tile_host). The real watchdog behavior remains covered by fake_async tests (which don't install a test binding). Confirmed root cause. Both failing tests are the same pattern:

1. **shard 0**: `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` — "first boot: onboarding → skip → setup → connect → launcher home" — pending 10s restore Timer created by `beginRestore()` from `_boot()` (via `_onboardingFinished`).
2. **shard 1**: `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` — "a restorable connection boots straight to the spinner" — pending 10s restore Timer created by `beginRestore()` from `_boot()` (via `initState` post-frame).

Both fail with "A Timer is still pending even after the widget tree was disposed" (`!timersPending`).

Why is the timer still pending? In both cases, `_boot()`'s restore chain is in flight when the test body completes:
- Test 2 ("boots straight to the spinner"): the test pumps the BootstrapScreen, the post-frame `_boot()` starts the restore (arms the 10s timer), and the test asserts the spinner is showing — the restore is INTENTIONALLY still in flight when the test ends. `restoreDone()` never runs because the restore hasn't completed. The 10s timer remains pending → invariant violation.
- Test 1 (boot_flows first boot): taps through onboarding → setup → connect → launcher home. `_onboardingFinished` → `_boot()` arms the restore timer; the test reaches launcher home... but the pending timer suggests the `_boot()` future never completed within the test's fake-async lifetime. Possibly the restore chain is stuck awaiting something (the test environment stalls it — e.g. an agent service awaiting network that never completes under the test binding), or the test ends before the chain drains. Either way, the timer is still armed at test end.

Now — the fix. Options:

**Option A: Make the watchdog test-aware.** In test environments (`Platform.environment.containsKey('FLUTTER_TEST')`), skip arming or use zero durations. But the pending-timer invariant would still trip if we arm timers in testWidgets... Well, if we don't arm at all under FLUTTER_TEST, no timers, tests pass. But then the boot tests wouldn't exercise the watchdog — that's what the dedicated boot_watchdog_test.dart with fakeAsync is for. This is a common pattern (CI-only guards exist elsewhere in this repo: `native_test_guard.dart` etc.).

**Option B: In `_boot()`, disarm more aggressively** — restoreDone() in finally already runs when the chain completes; the problem is tests that END while the chain is in flight. Can't fix from production code — the test ends mid-flight by design ("boots straight to the spinner").

**Option C: Use `Timer` with `FakeAsync`-friendly API**... no such thing.

The right fix per repo conventions: check how other boot-path timers handle this. E.g. "skill seeding 5 s timeout", "180 s provider connect watchdog" — how do they avoid pending-timer failures in widget tests? blocks.text:
The app_boot_test.dart exercises `FaAppBoot.run()` with `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized()`. With the PR's change, `run()` calls `kBootWatchdog.install()` which schedules `addPostFrameCallback` and arms a real 4s `Timer`. In a plain `test()` (not `testWidgets`), a real Timer of 4 seconds may fire if the test takes >4s... and `firstFrame()` would be called only when a frame lands — in a non-widget test no frame ever lands. The watchdog timer would fire at 4s and log a breadcrumb ("first frame not reached..."). Then re-arm every 30s up to 10 firings. That's harmless for the test itself unless the test framework complains about pending timers at the end of a `testWidgets` body... but these are plain `test()` bodies.

Hmm, but wait — `runWithEnv` test: `install()` called → `addPostFrameCallback` on TestWidgetsFlutterBinding. With FakeAsync? Plain `test()` in flutter_test runs in a normal zone. A pending Timer at the end of a plain test is NOT an error (unlike testWidgets which fails with "A Timer is still pending"). So that shouldn't fail.

Let me now check the progress of the background shards and, meanwhile, think about what else could be red.

Actually — hold on. Let me reconsider the failing checks:
- "Flutter app tests (shard 1/2)" — failure
- "Flutter app tests (shard 0/2)" — failure
- "Quality gate" — failure (aggregate)

Both shards red. If it were the boot watchdog tests, they'd all be in one shard (same directory, sorted adjacent → same shard). Something failing in BOTH shards = either (a) compile error affecting many tests, or (b) a widespread infra failure (e.g. pub get failure, firebase_options template missing, .env placeholder missing), or (c) two different genuine failures.

Since analyze passes locally with pub get done, and CI does the same steps... Actually wait — does CI's `flutter-analyze` leg also run on this head? It's in the needs list of quality-gate; only 3 checks failed: quality-gate, flutter-tests 0/2, 1/2. flutter-analyze must have passed (otherwise it'd be listed too). So code compiles. Runtime failures in both shards then.

Interesting: could this be the "timeout-minutes: 20" being hit? "End-of-run drain can stall minutes under shared-runner load" — timeout would mark the job failed without specific test failures. Or maybe the coverage upload step, or the fastlane step (shard 0 only)... but shard 1 also failed.

The arm64 runner (ubuntu-24.04-arm): "Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)" clones flutter stable. If the clone or precache failed (network flake), the job fails early. That could redden both shards as infra flake.

Confirmed root cause. Both failing tests are the same pattern:

1. **shard 0**: `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` — "first boot: onboarding → skip → setup → connect → launcher home" — pending 10s restore Timer created by `beginRestore()` from `_boot()` (via `_onboardingFinished`).
2. **shard 1**: `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` — "a restorable connection boots straight to the spinner" — pending 10s restore Timer created by `beginRestore()` from `_boot()` (via `initState` post-frame).

Both fail with "A Timer is still pending even after the widget tree was disposed" (`!timersPending`).

Why is the timer still pending? In both cases, `_boot()`'s restore chain is in flight when the test body completes:
- Test 2 ("boots straight to the spinner"): the test pumps the BootstrapScreen, the post-frame `_boot()` starts the restore (arms the 10s timer), and the test asserts the spinner is showing — the restore is INTENTIONALLY still in flight when the test ends. `restoreDone()` never runs because the restore hasn't completed. The 10s timer remains pending → invariant violation.
- Test 1 (boot_flows first boot): taps through onboarding → setup → connect → launcher home. `_onboardingFinished` → `_boot()` arms the restore timer; the test reaches launcher home... but the pending timer suggests the `_boot()` future never completed within the test's fake-async lifetime. Possibly the restore chain is stuck awaiting something (the test environment stalls it — e.g. an agent service awaiting network that never completes under the test binding), or the test ends before the chain drains. Either way, the timer is still armed at test end.

Now — the fix. Options:

**Option A: Make the watchdog test-aware.** In test environments (`Platform.environment.containsKey('FLUTTER_TEST')`), skip arming or use zero durations. But the pending-timer invariant would still trip if we arm timers in testWidgets... Well, if we don't arm at all under FLUTTER_TEST, no timers, tests pass. But then the boot tests wouldn't exercise the watchdog — that's what the dedicated boot_watchdog_test.dart with fakeAsync is for. This is a common pattern (CI-only guards exist elsewhere in this repo: `native_test_guard.dart` etc.).

**Option B: In `_boot()`, disarm more aggressively** — restoreDone() in finally already runs when the chain completes; the problem is tests that END while the chain is in flight. Can't fix from production code — the test ends mid-flight by design ("boots straight to the spinner").

**Option C: Use `Timer` with `FakeAsync`-friendly API**... no such thing.

```
❌ flutter_app/test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart: boot flows first boot: onboarding → skip → setup → connect → launcher home; the key never reaches last_connection.json (failed)
```

with:

```
Failed assertion: line 2543 pos 12: '!timersPending'
```

That's the classic `testWidgets` failure: "A Timer is still pending even after the widget tree was disposed" — `!timersPending` assertion at widget_tester line 2543. The PR's watchdog arms a real 4-second Timer via `install()`, which runs during boot flows in `testWidgets` tests — at the end of the test body, pending timers fail the test!

That's exactly the regression: `kBootWatchdog.install()` in `FaAppBoot.run()` arms `Timer(threshold)` and `addPostFrameCallback`. In `testWidgets`-based integration tests (boot_flows_test.dart) that pump the app (BootstrapScreen → which constructs FaAppBoot or calls main()), the pending watchdog timer trips the framework's "!timersPending" assertion when the test completes.
