{"content":"## Validation CI red on `cd2d3f39` — fixed: boot watchdog left pending timers in widget tests + restore phase never disarmed on a healthy boot

### Issues/Notes

- Validation CI failed on head `cd2d3f39` in **both** `Flutter app tests` shards (the `Quality gate` failure is just the aggregate of those two legs). `ci_failures_full.log` was not present locally; root cause was recovered from the failed jobs' logs (run 38364224395, jobs 115185593321 / 115185593401) and reproduced locally (1 failure per shard, same tests).
- Both failures were the flutter_test `!timersPending` invariant — `A Timer is still pending even after the widget tree was disposed`:
  - `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` — "first boot: onboarding → skip → setup → connect → launcher home"
  - `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` — "a restorable connection boots straight to the spinner"
- The pending timer was the watchdog's **restore-phase 10 s timer**, exposed by two defects in the restore-phase wiring (added by the earlier review-thread fix):
  1. `_boot()` disarmed the phase in a `finally` **after** `await navigator.pushReplacement(...)` — that future stays pending for as long as the user sits on home (and `bootExtensionRelay` awaits `onHome`, which awaits the same navigation). So on every **healthy** launch the restore phase stayed armed for the whole session: production would log spurious `restore not completed` breadcrumbs from 10 s after every boot (×10 + a `giving up` line), and widget tests that end parked on home died on the pending timer.
  2. The spinner-shaped test ends **while the restore is intentionally still in flight** — with real watchdog timers inside `testWidgets` boot flows, no disarm placement can save that test; the binding fails any test that ends with timers pending.
- Note: `flutter analyze` on this head is clean (no errors); the two lints in `flutter_app/test/boot/` (unused `fa/main.dart` import — pre-existing on `main`; `fake_async` not a declared dev-dep — info-level, analyze leg already green on CI) are out of scope for this fix.

### Approach

- **`flutter_app/lib/main.dart`** — disarm the restore phase when the *restore* ends, not when the navigation ends: `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` now runs right after `BootSteps.mark('restore:session')` and at the top of `_bootRelay`'s `onHome` (both before the `pushReplacement` await). The `finally` blocks remain as the failure-path net (`restoreDone` is idempotent): a restore that threw — landing on the setup form, no wedge — is still disarmed on the way out, so the review thread's post-frame coverage is unchanged for real wedges and no longer spams healthy launches.
- **`flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart`** — `BootWatchdog` now takes `bool? timersEnabled`, defaulting to "armed everywhere EXCEPT under a `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding`" (same binding-name probe as `app_tile_host.dart`, which documents the identical `!timersPending` failure mode). Under tests the phases are still recorded (`beginRestore`/`restoreDone` bookkeeping, `describe()` context) but no real timer exists — nothing can fire, nothing is left pending. Release builds never run under a test binding, so production always arms. `install()` idempotency now keys on an `_installed` flag (a second install stays a no-op even when timers are disarmed).
- **`flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`** — the fake_async suite opts back into real timers (`timersEnabled: true` at all 6 construction sites) and gained 3 regression tests:
  - `a successful restore stays silent while the user sits on home` (the `_boot` wiring contract pinned above)
  - `the default watchdog arms no timers — nothing left pending` (direct regression for the CI red; pre-fix it fires the restore breadcrumb / dies on the invariant)
  - `timersEnabled: true opts a test-hosted instance back in`

### Files Modified

- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` — `timersEnabled` (test-binding-aware default), `_arm` guard, `_installed` idempotency flag, docs (library + class).
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart` — `_boot()` / `_bootRelay()`: `restoreDone()` at restore completion instead of post-navigation; `finally` kept as failure-path net.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` — `timersEnabled: true` opt-in ×6, +3 regression tests.

### Test Coverage

- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`: **19/19 PASS** (was 16).
- Previously-failing suites re-run locally with the CI shard recipe (`--exclude-tags integration`, non-golden/non-`cli_visual`): `test/boot/` + `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` + `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` → **68/68 PASS** (both formerly-red tests green).
- Full CI-equivalent shard verification (`find test … NR % 2 == shard`, both shards, with `FA_*` shell vars unset — this runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` otherwise leaks into `providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart`, as noted in the PR description): **shard 0: 1786 passed, 91 skipped, 0 failed; shard 1: 1908 passed, 17 skipped, 0 failed.**
- `flutter analyze` on `flutter_app`: no errors.

{"content":"## Validation CI red on `cd2d3f39` — fixed: boot watchdog left pending timers in widget tests + restore phase never disarmed on a healthy boot

### Issues/Notes

- Validation CI failed on head `cd2d3f39` in **both** `Flutter app tests` shards (the `Quality gate` failure is just the aggregate of those two legs). `ci_failures_full.log` was not present locally; root cause was recovered from the failed jobs' logs (run 38364224395, jobs 115185593321 / 115185593401) and reproduced locally (1 failure per shard, same tests).
- Both failures were the flutter_test `!timersPending` invariant — `A Timer is still pending even after the widget tree was disposed`:
  - `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` — "first boot: onboarding → skip → setup → connect → launcher home"
  - `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` — "a restorable connection boots straight to the spinner"
- The pending timer was the watchdog's **restore-phase 10 s timer**, exposed by two defects in the restore-phase wiring (added by the earlier review-thread fix):
  1. `_boot()` disarmed the phase in a `finally` **after** `await navigator.pushReplacement(...)` — that future stays pending for as long as the user sits on home (and `bootExtensionRelay` awaits `onHome`, which awaits the same navigation). So on every **healthy** launch the restore phase stayed armed for the whole session: production would log spurious `restore not completed` breadcrumbs from 10 s after every boot (×10 + a `giving up` line), and widget tests that end parked on home died on the pending timer.
  2. The spinner-shaped test ends **while the restore is intentionally still in flight** — with real watchdog timers inside `testWidgets` boot flows, no disarm placement can save that test; the binding fails any test that ends with timers pending.
- Note: `flutter analyze` on this head is clean (no errors); the two lints in `flutter_app/test/boot/` (unused `fa/main.dart` import — pre-existing on `main`; `fake_async` not a declared dev-dep — info-level, analyze leg already green on CI) are out of scope for this fix.

### Approach

- **`flutter_app/lib/main.dart`** — disarm the restore phase when the *restore* ends, not when the navigation ends: `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` now runs right after `BootSteps.mark('restore:session')` and at the top of `_bootRelay`'s `onHome` (both before the `pushReplacement` await). The `finally` blocks remain as the failure-path net (`restoreDone` is idempotent): a restore that threw — landing on the setup form, no wedge — is still disarmed on the way out, so the review thread's post-frame coverage is unchanged for real wedges and no longer spams healthy launches.
- **`flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart`** — `BootWatchdog` now takes `bool? timersEnabled`, defaulting to "armed everywhere EXCEPT under a `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding`" (same binding-name probe as `app_tile_host.dart`, which documents the identical `!timersPending` failure mode). Under tests the phases are still recorded (`beginRestore`/`restoreDone` bookkeeping, `describe()` context) but no real timer exists — nothing can fire, nothing is left pending. Release builds never run under a test binding, so production always arms. `install()` idempotency now keys on an `_installed` flag (a second install stays a no-op even when timers are disarmed).
- **`flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`** — the fake_async suite opts back into real timers (`timersEnabled: true` at all 6 construction sites) and gained 3 regression tests:
  - `a successful restore stays silent while the user sits on home` (the `_boot` wiring contract pinned above)
  - `the default watchdog arms no timers — nothing left pending` (direct regression for the CI red; pre-fix it fires the restore breadcrumb / dies on the invariant)
  - `timersEnabled: true opts a test-hosted instance back in`

### Files Modified

- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` — `timersEnabled` (test-binding-aware default), `_arm` guard, `_installed` idempotency flag, docs (library + class).
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart` — `_boot()` / `_bootRelay()`: `restoreDone()` at restore completion instead of post-navigation; `finally` kept as failure-path net.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` — `timersEnabled: true` opt-in ×6, +3 regression tests.

### Test Coverage

- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`: **19/19 PASS** (was 16).
- Previously-failing suites re-run locally with the CI shard recipe (`--exclude-tags integration`, non-golden/non-`cli_visual`): `test/boot/` + `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` + `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` → **68/68 PASS** (both formerly-red tests green).
- Full CI-equivalent shard verification (`find test … NR % 2 == shard`, both shards, with `FA_*` shell vars unset — this runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` otherwise leaks into `providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart`, as noted in the PR description): **shard 0: 1786 passed, 91 skipped, 0 failed; shard 1: 1908 passed, 17 skipped, 0 failed.**
- `flutter analyze` on `flutter_app`: no errors.

{"content":"## Validation CI red on `cd2d3f39` — fixed: boot watchdog left pending timers in widget tests + restore phase never disarmed on a healthy boot

### Issues/Notes

- Validation CI failed on head `cd2d3f39` in **both** `Flutter app tests` shards (the `Quality gate` failure is just the aggregate of those two legs). `ci_failures_full.log` was not present locally; root cause was recovered from the failed jobs' logs (run 38364224395, jobs 115185593321 / 115185593401) and reproduced locally (1 failure per shard, same tests).
- Both failures were the flutter_test `!timersPending` invariant — `A Timer is still pending even after the widget tree was disposed`:
  - `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` — "first boot: onboarding → skip → setup → connect → launcher home"
  - `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` — "a restorable connection boots straight to the spinner"
- The pending timer was the watchdog's **restore-phase 10 s timer**, exposed by two defects in the restore-phase wiring (added by the earlier review-thread fix):
  1. `_boot()` disarmed the phase in a `finally` **after** `await navigator.pushReplacement(...)` — that future stays pending for as long as the user sits on home (and `bootExtensionRelay` awaits `onHome`, which awaits the same navigation). So on every **healthy** launch the restore phase stayed armed for the whole session: production would log spurious `restore not completed` breadcrumbs from 10 s after every boot (×10 + a `giving up` line), and widget tests that end parked on home died on the pending timer.
  2. The spinner-shaped test ends **while the restore is intentionally still in flight** — with real watchdog timers inside `testWidgets` boot flows, no disarm placement can save that test; the binding fails any test that ends with timers pending.
- Note: `flutter analyze` on this head is clean (no errors); the two lints in `flutter_app/test/boot/` (unused `fa/main.dart` import — pre-existing on `main`; `fake_async` not a declared dev-dep — info-level, analyze leg already green on CI) are out of scope for this fix.

### Approach

- **`flutter_app/lib/main.dart`** — disarm the restore phase when the *restore* ends, not when the navigation ends: `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` now runs right after `BootSteps.mark('restore:session')` and at the top of `_bootRelay`'s `onHome` (both before the `pushReplacement` await). The `finally` blocks remain as the failure-path net (`restoreDone` is idempotent): a restore that threw — landing on the setup form, no wedge — is still disarmed on the way out, so the review thread's post-frame coverage is unchanged for real wedges and no longer spams healthy launches.
- **`flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart`** — `BootWatchdog` now takes `bool? timersEnabled`, defaulting to "armed everywhere EXCEPT under a `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding`" (same binding-name probe as `app_tile_host.dart`, which documents the identical `!timersPending` failure mode). Under tests the phases are still recorded (`beginRestore`/`restoreDone` bookkeeping, `describe()` context) but no real timer exists — nothing can fire, nothing is left pending. Release builds never run under a test binding, so production always arms. `install()` idempotency now keys on an `_installed` flag (a second install stays a no-op even when timers are disarmed).
- **`flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`** — the fake_async suite opts back into real timers (`timersEnabled: true` at all 6 construction sites) and gained 3 regression tests:
  - `a successful restore stays silent while the user sits on home` (the `_boot` wiring contract pinned above)
  - `the default watchdog arms no timers — nothing left pending` (direct regression for the CI red; pre-fix it fires the restore breadcrumb / dies on the invariant)
  - `timersEnabled: true opts a test-hosted instance back in`

### Files Modified

- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` — `timersEnabled` (test-binding-aware default), `_arm` guard, `_installed` idempotency flag, docs (library + class).
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart` — `_boot()` / `_bootRelay()`: `restoreDone()` at restore completion instead of post-navigation; `finally` kept as failure-path net.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` — `timersEnabled: true` opt-in ×6, +3 regression tests.

### Test Coverage

- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`: **19/19 PASS** (was 16).
- Previously-failing suites re-run locally with the CI shard recipe (`--exclude-tags integration`, non-golden/non-`cli_visual`): `test/boot/` + `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` + `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` → **68/68 PASS** (both formerly-red tests green).
- Full CI-equivalent shard verification (`find test … NR % 2 == shard`, both shards, with `FA_*` shell vars unset — this runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` otherwise leaks into `providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart`, as noted in the PR description): **shard 0: 1786 passed, 91 skipped, 0 failed; shard 1: 1908 passed, 17 skipped, 0 failed.**
- `flutter analyze` on `flutter_app`: no errors.

- Both failures were the flutter_test `!timersPending` invariant — `A Timer is still pending even after the widget tree was disposed`:
  - `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` — "first boot: onboarding → skip → setup → connect → launcher home"
  - `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` — "a restorable connection boots straight to the spinner"
- The pending timer was the watchdog's **restore-phase 10 s timer**, exposed by two defects in the restore-phase wiring (added by the earlier review-thread fix):
  1. `_boot()` disarmed the phase in a `finally` **after** `await navigator.pushReplacement(...)` — that future stays pending for as long as the user sits on home (and `bootExtensionRelay` awaits `onHome`, which awaits the same navigation). So on every **healthy** launch the restore phase stayed armed for the whole session: production would log spurious `restore not completed` breadcrumbs from 10 s after every boot (×10 + a `giving up` line), and widget tests that end parked on home died on the pending timer.
  2. The spinner-shaped test ends **while the restore is intentionally still in flight** — with real watchdog timers inside `testWidgets` boot flows, no disarm placement can save that test; the binding fails any test that ends with timers pending.
- Note: `flutter analyze` on this head is clean (no errors); the two lints in `flutter_app/test/boot/` (unused `fa/main.dart` import — pre-existing on `main`; `fake_async` not a declared dev-dep — info-level, analyze leg already green on CI) are out of scope for this fix.

### Approach

- **`flutter_app/lib/main.dart`** — disarm the restore phase when the *restore* ends, not when the navigation ends: `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` now runs right after `BootSteps.mark('restore:session')` and at the top of `_bootRelay`'s `onHome` (both before the `pushReplacement` await). The `finally` blocks remain as the failure-path net (`restoreDone` is idempotent): a restore that threw — landing on the setup form, no wedge — is still disarmed on the way out, so the review thread's post-frame coverage is unchanged for real wedges and no longer spams healthy launches.
- **`flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart`** — `BootWatchdog` now takes `bool? timersEnabled`, defaulting to "armed everywhere EXCEPT under a `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding`" (same binding-name probe as `app_tile_host.dart`, which documents the identical `!timersPending` failure mode). Under tests the phases are still recorded (`beginRestore`/`restoreDone` bookkeeping, `describe()` context) but no real timer exists — nothing can fire, nothing is left pending. Release builds never run under a test binding, so production always arms. `install()` idempotency now keys on an `_installed` flag (a second install stays a no-op even when timers are disarmed).
- **`flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`** — the fake_async suite opts back into real timers (`timersEnabled: true` at all 6 construction sites) and gained 3 regression tests:
  - `a successful restore stays silent while the user sits on home` (the `_boot` wiring contract pinned above)
  - `the default watchdog arms no timers — nothing left pending` (direct regression for the CI red; pre-fix it fires the restore breadcrumb / dies on the invariant)
  - `timersEnabled: true opts a test-hosted instance back in`

### Files Modified

- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` — `timersEnabled` (test-binding-aware default), `_arm` guard, `_installed` idempotency flag, docs (library + class).
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart` — `_boot()` / `_bootRelay()`: `restoreDone()` at restore completion instead of post-navigation; `finally` kept as failure-path net.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` — `timersEnabled: true` opt-in ×6, +3 regression tests.

### Test Coverage

- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`: **19/19 PASS** (was 16).
- Previously-failing suites re-run locally with the CI shard recipe (`--exclude-tags integration`, non-golden/non-`cli_visual`): `test/boot/` + `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` + `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` → **68/68 PASS** (both formerly-red tests green).

{"content":"## Validation CI red on `cd2d3f39` — fixed: boot watchdog left pending timers in widget tests + restore phase never disarmed on a healthy boot

### Issues/Notes

- Validation CI failed on head `cd2d3f39` in **both** `Flutter app tests` shards (the `Quality gate` failure is just the aggregate of those two legs). `ci_failures_full.log` was not present locally; root cause was recovered from the failed jobs' logs (run 38364224395, jobs 115185593321 / 115185593401) and reproduced locally (1 failure per shard, same tests).
- Both failures were the flutter_test `!timersPending` invariant — `A Timer is still pending even after the widget tree was disposed`:
  - `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` — "first boot: onboarding → skip → setup → connect → launcher home"
  - `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` — "a restorable connection boots straight to the spinner"
- The pending timer was the watchdog's **restore-phase 10 s timer**, exposed by two defects in the restore-phase wiring (added by the earlier review-thread fix):
  1. `_boot()` disarmed the phase in a `finally` **after** `await navigator.pushReplacement(...)` — that future stays pending for as long as the user sits on home (and `bootExtensionRelay` awaits `onHome`, which awaits the same navigation). So on every **healthy** launch the restore phase stayed armed for the whole session: production would log spurious `restore not completed` breadcrumbs from 10 s after every boot (×10 + a `giving up` line), and widget tests that end parked on home died on the pending timer.
  2. The spinner-shaped test ends **while the restore is intentionally still in flight** — with real watchdog timers inside `testWidgets` boot flows, no disarm placement can save that test; the binding fails any test that ends with timers pending.
- Note: `flutter analyze` on this head is clean (no errors); the two lints in `flutter_app/test/boot/` (unused `fa/main.dart` import — pre-existing on `main`; `fake_async` not a declared dev-dep — info-level, analyze leg already green on CI) are out of scope for this fix.

### Approach

- **`flutter_app/lib/main.dart`** — disarm the restore phase when the *restore* ends, not when the navigation ends: `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` now runs right after `BootSteps.mark('restore:session')` and at the top of `_bootRelay`'s `onHome` (both before the `pushReplacement` await). The `finally` blocks remain as the failure-path net (`restoreDone` is idempotent): a restore that threw — landing on the setup form, no wedge — is still disarmed on the way out, so the review thread's post-frame coverage is unchanged for real wedges and no longer spams healthy launches.
- **`flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart`** — `BootWatchdog` now takes `bool? timersEnabled`, defaulting to "armed everywhere EXCEPT under a `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding`" (same binding-name probe as `app_tile_host.dart`, which documents the identical `!timersPending` failure mode). Under tests the phases are still recorded (`beginRestore`/`restoreDone` bookkeeping, `describe()` context) but no real timer exists — nothing can fire, nothing is left pending. Release builds never run under a test binding, so production always arms. `install()` idempotency now keys on an `_installed` flag (a second install stays a no-op even when timers are disarmed).
- **`flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`** — the fake_async suite opts back into real timers (`timersEnabled: true` at all 6 construction sites) and gained 3 regression tests:
  - `a successful restore stays silent while the user sits on home` (the `_boot` wiring contract pinned above)
  - `the default watchdog arms no timers — nothing left pending` (direct regression for the CI red; pre-fix it fires the restore breadcrumb / dies on the invariant)
  - `timersEnabled: true opts a test-hosted instance back in`

### Files Modified

- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` — `timersEnabled` (test-binding-aware default), `_arm` guard, `_installed` idempotency flag, docs (library + class).
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart` — `_boot()` / `_bootRelay()`: `restoreDone()` at restore completion instead of post-navigation; `finally` kept as failure-path net.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` — `timersEnabled: true` opt-in ×6, +3 regression tests.

### Test Coverage

- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`: **19/19 PASS** (was 16).
- Previously-failing suites re-run locally with the CI shard recipe (`--exclude-tags integration`, non-golden/non-`cli_visual`): `test/boot/` + `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` + `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` → **68/68 PASS** (both formerly-red tests green).

{"content":"## Validation CI red on `cd2d3f39` — fixed: boot watchdog left pending timers in widget tests + restore phase never disarmed on a healthy boot

### Issues/Notes

- Validation CI failed on head `cd2d3f39` in **both** `Flutter app tests` shards (the `Quality gate` failure is just the aggregate of those two legs). `ci_failures_full.log` was not present locally; root cause was recovered from the failed jobs' logs (run 38364224395, jobs 115185593321 / 115185593401) and reproduced locally (1 failure per shard, same tests).
- Both failures were the flutter_test `!timersPending` invariant — `A Timer is still pending even after the widget tree was disposed`:
  - `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` — "first boot: onboarding → skip → setup → connect → launcher home"
  - `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` — "a restorable connection boots straight to the spinner"
- The pending timer was the watchdog's **restore-phase 10 s timer**, exposed by two defects in the restore-phase wiring (added by the earlier review-thread fix):
  1. `_boot()` disarmed the phase in a `finally` **after** `await navigator.pushReplacement(...)` — that future stays pending for as long as the user sits on home (and `bootExtensionRelay` awaits `onHome`, which awaits the same navigation). So on every **healthy** launch the restore phase stayed armed for the whole session: production would log spurious `restore not completed` breadcrumbs from 10 s after every boot (×10 + a `giving up` line), and widget tests that end parked on home died on the pending timer.
  2. The spinner-shaped test ends **while the restore is intentionally still in flight** — with real watchdog timers inside `testWidgets` boot flows, no disarm placement can save that test; the binding fails any test that ends with timers pending.
- Note: `flutter analyze` on this head is clean (no errors); the two lints in `flutter_app/test/boot/` (unused `fa/main.dart` import — pre-existing on `main`; `fake_async` not a declared dev-dep — info-level, analyze leg already green on CI) are out of scope for this fix.

### Approach

- **`flutter_app/lib/main.dart`** — disarm the restore phase when the *restore* ends, not when the navigation ends: `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` now runs right after `BootSteps.mark('restore:session')` and at the top of `_bootRelay`'s `onHome` (both before the `pushReplacement` await). The `finally` blocks remain as the failure-path net (`restoreDone` is idempotent): a restore that threw — landing on the setup form, no wedge — is still disarmed on the way out, so the review thread's post-frame coverage is unchanged for real wedges and no longer spams healthy launches.
- **`flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart`** — `BootWatchdog` now takes `bool? timersEnabled`, defaulting to "armed everywhere EXCEPT under a `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding`" (same binding-name probe as `app_tile_host.dart`, which documents the identical `!timersPending` failure mode). Under tests the phases are still recorded (`beginRestore`/`restoreDone` bookkeeping, `describe()` context) but no real timer exists — nothing can fire, nothing is left pending. Release builds never run under a test binding, so production always arms. `install()` idempotency now keys on an `_installed` flag (a second install stays a no-op even when timers are disarmed).
- **`flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`** — the fake_async suite opts back into real timers (`timersEnabled: true` at all 6 construction sites) and gained 3 regression tests:
  - `a successful restore stays silent while the user sits on home` (the `_boot` wiring contract pinned above)
  - `the default watchdog arms no timers — nothing left pending` (direct regression for the CI red; pre-fix it fires the restore breadcrumb / dies on the invariant)
  - `timersEnabled: true opts a test-hosted instance back in`

### Files Modified

- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` — `timersEnabled` (test-binding-aware default), `_arm` guard, `_installed` idempotency flag, docs (library + class).
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart` — `_boot()` / `_bootRelay()`: `restoreDone()` at restore completion instead of post-navigation; `finally` kept as failure-path net.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` — `timersEnabled: true` opt-in ×6, +3 regression tests.

### Test Coverage

- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`: **19/19 PASS** (was 16).
- Previously-failing suites re-run locally with the CI shard recipe (`--exclude-tags integration`, non-golden/non-`cli_visual`): `test/boot/` + `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` + `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` → **68/68 PASS** (both formerly-red tests green).
- Full CI-equivalent shard verification (`find test … NR % 2 == shard`, both shards, with `FA_*` shell vars unset — this runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` otherwise leaks into `providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart`, as noted in the PR description): **shard 0: 1786 passed, 91 skipped, 0 failed; shard 1: 1908 passed, 17 skipped, 0 failed.**
- `flutter analyze` on `flutter_app`: no errors.

{"content":"## Validation CI red on `cd2d3f39` — fixed: boot watchdog left pending timers in widget tests + restore phase never disarmed on a healthy boot

### Issues/Notes

- Validation CI failed on head `cd2d3f39` in **both** `Flutter app tests` shards (the `Quality gate` failure is just the aggregate of those two legs). `ci_failures_full.log` was not present locally; root cause was recovered from the failed jobs' logs (run 38364224395, jobs 115185593321 / 115185593401) and reproduced locally (1 failure per shard, same tests).
- Both failures were the flutter_test `!timersPending` invariant — `A Timer is still pending even after the widget tree was disposed`:
  - `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` — "first boot: onboarding → skip → setup → connect → launcher home"
  - `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` — "a restorable connection boots straight to the spinner"
- The pending timer was the watchdog's **restore-phase 10 s timer**, exposed by two defects in the restore-phase wiring (added by the earlier review-thread fix):
  1. `_boot()` disarmed the phase in a `finally` **after** `await navigator.pushReplacement(...)` — that future stays pending for as long as the user sits on home (and `bootExtensionRelay` awaits `onHome`, which awaits the same navigation). So on every **healthy** launch the restore phase stayed armed for the whole session: production would log spurious `restore not completed` breadcrumbs from 10 s after every boot (×10 + a `giving up` line), and widget tests that end parked on home died on the pending timer.
  2. The spinner-shaped test ends **while the restore is intentionally still in flight** — with real watchdog timers inside `testWidgets` boot flows, no disarm placement can save that test; the binding fails any test that ends with timers pending.
- Note: `flutter analyze` on this head is clean (no errors); the two lints in `flutter_app/test/boot/` (unused `fa/main.dart` import — pre-existing on `main`; `fake_async` not a declared dev-dep — info-level, analyze leg already green on CI) are out of scope for this fix.

### Approach

- **`flutter_app/lib/main.dart`** — disarm the restore phase when the *restore* ends, not when the navigation ends: `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` now runs right after `BootSteps.mark('restore:session')` and at the top of `_bootRelay`'s `onHome` (both before the `pushReplacement` await). The `finally` blocks remain as the failure-path net (`restoreDone` is idempotent): a restore that threw — landing on the setup form, no wedge — is still disarmed on the way out, so the review thread's post-frame coverage is unchanged for real wedges and no longer spams healthy launches.
- **`flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart`** — `BootWatchdog` now takes `bool? timersEnabled`, defaulting to "armed everywhere EXCEPT under a `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding`" (same binding-name probe as `app_tile_host.dart`, which documents the identical `!timersPending` failure mode). Under tests the phases are still recorded (`beginRestore`/`restoreDone` bookkeeping, `describe()` context) but no real timer exists — nothing can fire, nothing is left pending. Release builds never run under a test binding, so production always arms. `install()` idempotency now keys on an `_installed` flag (a second install stays a no-op even when timers are disarmed).
- **`flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`** — the fake_async suite opts back into real timers (`timersEnabled: true` at all 6 construction sites) and gained 3 regression tests:
  - `a successful restore stays silent while the user sits on home` (the `_boot` wiring contract pinned above)
  - `the default watchdog arms no timers — nothing left pending` (direct regression for the CI red; pre-fix it fires the restore breadcrumb / dies on the invariant)
  - `timersEnabled: true opts a test-hosted instance back in`

### Files Modified

- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` — `timersEnabled` (test-binding-aware default), `_arm` guard, `_installed` idempotency flag, docs (library + class).
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart` — `_boot()` / `_bootRelay()`: `restoreDone()` at restore completion instead of post-navigation; `finally` kept as failure-path net.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` — `timersEnabled: true` opt-in ×6, +3 regression tests.

### Test Coverage

{"content":"## Validation CI red on `cd2d3f39` — fixed: boot watchdog left pending timers in widget tests + restore phase never disarmed on a healthy boot

### Issues/Notes

- Validation CI failed on head `cd2d3f39` in **both** `Flutter app tests` shards (the `Quality gate` failure is just the aggregate of those two legs). `ci_failures_full.log` was not present locally; root cause was recovered from the failed jobs' logs (run 38364224395, jobs 115185593321 / 115185593401) and reproduced locally (1 failure per shard, same tests).
- Both failures were the flutter_test `!timersPending` invariant — `A Timer is still pending even after the widget tree was disposed`:
  - `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` — "first boot: onboarding → skip → setup → connect → launcher home"
  - `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` — "a restorable connection boots straight to the spinner"
- The pending timer was the watchdog's **restore-phase 10 s timer**, exposed by two defects in the restore-phase wiring (added by the earlier review-thread fix):
  1. `_boot()` disarmed the phase in a `finally` **after** `await navigator.pushReplacement(...)` — that future stays pending for as long as the user sits on home (and `bootExtensionRelay` awaits `onHome`, which awaits the same navigation). So on every **healthy** launch the restore phase stayed armed for the whole session: production would log spurious `restore not completed` breadcrumbs from 10 s after every boot (×10 + a `giving up` line), and widget tests that end parked on home died on the pending timer.
  2. The spinner-shaped test ends **while the restore is intentionally still in flight** — with real watchdog timers inside `testWidgets` boot flows, no disarm placement can save that test; the binding fails any test that ends with timers pending.
- Note: `flutter analyze` on this head is clean (no errors); the two lints in `flutter_app/test/boot/` (unused `fa/main.dart` import — pre-existing on `main`; `fake_async` not a declared dev-dep — info-level, analyze leg already green on CI) are out of scope for this fix.

### Approach

- **`flutter_app/lib/main.dart`** — disarm the restore phase when the *restore* ends, not when the navigation ends: `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` now runs right after `BootSteps.mark('restore:session')` and at the top of `_bootRelay`'s `onHome` (both before the `pushReplacement` await). The `finally` blocks remain as the failure-path net (`restoreDone` is idempotent): a restore that threw — landing on the setup form, no wedge — is still disarmed on the way out, so the review thread's post-frame coverage is unchanged for real wedges and no longer spams healthy launches.
- **`flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart`** — `BootWatchdog` now takes `bool? timersEnabled`, defaulting to "armed everywhere EXCEPT under a `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding`" (same binding-name probe as `app_tile_host.dart`, which documents the identical `!timersPending` failure mode). Under tests the phases are still recorded (`beginRestore`/`restoreDone` bookkeeping, `describe()` context) but no real timer exists — nothing can fire, nothing is left pending. Release builds never run under a test binding, so production always arms. `install()` idempotency now keys on an `_installed` flag (a second install stays a no-op even when timers are disarmed).
- **`flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`** — the fake_async suite opts back into real timers (`timersEnabled: true` at all 6 construction sites) and gained 3 regression tests:
  - `a successful restore stays silent while the user sits on home` (the `_boot` wiring contract pinned above)
  - `the default watchdog arms no timers — nothing left pending` (direct regression for the CI red; pre-fix it fires the restore breadcrumb / dies on the invariant)
  - `timersEnabled: true opts a test-hosted instance back in`

### Files Modified

- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` — `timersEnabled` (test-binding-aware default), `_arm` guard, `_installed` idempotency flag, docs (library + class).
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart` — `_boot()` / `_bootRelay()`: `restoreDone()` at restore completion instead of post-navigation; `finally` kept as failure-path net.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` — `timersEnabled: true` opt-in ×6, +3 regression tests.

### Test Coverage

- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`: **19/19 PASS** (was 16).
- Previously-failing suites re-run locally with the CI shard recipe (`--exclude-tags integration`, non-golden/non-`cli_visual`): `test/boot/` + `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` + `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` → **68/68 PASS** (both formerly-red tests green).
- Full CI-equivalent shard verification (`find test … NR % 2 == shard`, both shards, with `FA_*` shell vars unset — this runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` otherwise leaks into `providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart`, as noted in the PR description): **shard 0: 1786 passed, 91 skipped, 0 failed; shard 1: 1908 passed, 17 skipped, 0 failed.**
- `flutter analyze` on `flutter_app`: no errors.

{"content":"## Validation CI red on `cd2d3f39` — fixed: boot watchdog left pending timers in widget tests + restore phase never disarmed on a healthy boot

### Issues/Notes

- Validation CI failed on head `cd2d3f39` in **both** `Flutter app tests` shards (the `Quality gate` failure is just the aggregate of those two legs). `ci_failures_full.log` was not present locally; root cause was recovered from the failed jobs' logs (run 38364224395, jobs 115185593321 / 115185593401) and reproduced locally (1 failure per shard, same tests).
- Both failures were the flutter_test `!timersPending` invariant — `A Timer is still pending even after the widget tree was disposed`:
  - `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` — "first boot: onboarding → skip → setup → connect → launcher home"
  - `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` — "a restorable connection boots straight to the spinner"
- The pending timer was the watchdog's **restore-phase 10 s timer**, exposed by two defects in the restore-phase wiring (added by the earlier review-thread fix):
  1. `_boot()` disarmed the phase in a `finally` **after** `await navigator.pushReplacement(...)` — that future stays pending for as long as the user sits on home (and `bootExtensionRelay` awaits `onHome`, which awaits the same navigation). So on every **healthy** launch the restore phase stayed armed for the whole session: production would log spurious `restore not completed` breadcrumbs from 10 s after every boot (×10 + a `giving up` line), and widget tests that end parked on home died on the pending timer.
  2. The spinner-shaped test ends **while the restore is intentionally still in flight** — with real watchdog timers inside `testWidgets` boot flows, no disarm placement can save that test; the binding fails any test that ends with timers pending.
- Note: `flutter analyze` on this head is clean (no errors); the two lints in `flutter_app/test/boot/` (unused `fa/main.dart` import — pre-existing on `main`; `fake_async` not a declared dev-dep — info-level, analyze leg already green on CI) are out of scope for this fix.

### Approach

- **`flutter_app/lib/main.dart`** — disarm the restore phase when the *restore* ends, not when the navigation ends: `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` now runs right after `BootSteps.mark('restore:session')` and at the top of `_bootRelay`'s `onHome` (both before the `pushReplacement` await). The `finally` blocks remain as the failure-path net (`restoreDone` is idempotent): a restore that threw — landing on the setup form, no wedge — is still disarmed on the way out, so the review thread's post-frame coverage is unchanged for real wedges and no longer spams healthy launches.
- **`flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart`** — `BootWatchdog` now takes `bool? timersEnabled`, defaulting to "armed everywhere EXCEPT under a `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding`" (same binding-name probe as `app_tile_host.dart`, which documents the identical `!timersPending` failure mode). Under tests the phases are still recorded (`beginRestore`/`restoreDone` bookkeeping, `describe()` context) but no real timer exists — nothing can fire, nothing is left pending. Release builds never run under a test binding, so production always arms. `install()` idempotency now keys on an `_installed` flag (a second install stays a no-op even when timers are disarmed).
- **`flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`** — the fake_async suite opts back into real timers (`timersEnabled: true` at all 6 construction sites) and gained 3 regression tests:
  - `a successful restore stays silent while the user sits on home` (the `_boot` wiring contract pinned above)
  - `the default watchdog arms no timers — nothing left pending` (direct regression for the CI red; pre-fix it fires the restore breadcrumb / dies on the invariant)
  - `timersEnabled: true opts a test-hosted instance back in`

### Files Modified

- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` — `timersEnabled` (test-binding-aware default), `_arm` guard, `_installed` idempotency flag, docs (library + class).
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart` — `_boot()` / `_bootRelay()`: `restoreDone()` at restore completion instead of post-navigation; `finally` kept as failure-path net.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` — `timersEnabled: true` opt-in ×6, +3 regression tests.

### Test Coverage

- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`: **19/19 PASS** (was 16).
- Previously-failing suites re-run locally with the CI shard recipe (`--exclude-tags integration`, non-golden/non-`cli_visual`): `test/boot/` + `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` + `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` → **68/68 PASS** (both formerly-red tests green).

- `flutter analyze` on `flutter_app`: no errors.

{"content":"## Validation CI red on `cd2d3f39` — fixed: boot watchdog left pending timers in widget tests + restore phase never disarmed on a healthy boot

### Issues/Notes

- Validation CI failed on head `cd2d3f39` in **both** `Flutter app tests` shards (the `Quality gate` failure is just the aggregate of those two legs). `ci_failures_full.log` was not present locally; root cause was recovered from the failed jobs' logs (run 38364224395, jobs 115185593321 / 115185593401) and reproduced locally (1 failure per shard, same tests).
- Both failures were the flutter_test `!timersPending` invariant — `A Timer is still pending even after the widget tree was disposed`:
  - `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` — "first boot: onboarding → skip → setup → connect → launcher home"
  - `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` — "a restorable connection boots straight to the spinner"
- The pending timer was the watchdog's **restore-phase 10 s timer**, exposed by two defects in the restore-phase wiring (added by the earlier review-thread fix):
  1. `_boot()` disarmed the phase in a `finally` **after** `await navigator.pushReplacement(...)` — that future stays pending for as long as the user sits on home (and `bootExtensionRelay` awaits `onHome`, which awaits the same navigation). So on every **healthy** launch the restore phase stayed armed for the whole session: production would log spurious `restore not completed` breadcrumbs from 10 s after every boot (×10 + a `giving up` line), and widget tests that end parked on home died on the pending timer.
  2. The spinner-shaped test ends **while the restore is intentionally still in flight** — with real watchdog timers inside `testWidgets` boot flows, no disarm placement can save that test; the binding fails any test that ends with timers pending.
- Note: `flutter analyze` on this head is clean (no errors); the two lints in `flutter_app/test/boot/` (unused `fa/main.dart` import — pre-existing on `main`; `fake_async` not a declared dev-dep — info-level, analyze leg already green on CI) are out of scope for this fix.

### Approach

- **`flutter_app/lib/main.dart`** — disarm the restore phase when the *restore* ends, not when the navigation ends: `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` now runs right after `BootSteps.mark('restore:session')` and at the top of `_bootRelay`'s `onHome` (both before the `pushReplacement` await). The `finally` blocks remain as the failure-path net (`restoreDone` is idempotent): a restore that threw — landing on the setup form, no wedge — is still disarmed on the way out, so the review thread's post-frame coverage is unchanged for real wedges and no longer spams healthy launches.
- **`flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart`** — `BootWatchdog` now takes `bool? timersEnabled`, defaulting to "armed everywhere EXCEPT under a `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding`" (same binding-name probe as `app_tile_host.dart`, which documents the identical `!timersPending` failure mode). Under tests the phases are still recorded (`beginRestore`/`restoreDone` bookkeeping, `describe()` context) but no real timer exists — nothing can fire, nothing is left pending. Release builds never run under a test binding, so production always arms. `install()` idempotency now keys on an `_installed` flag (a second install stays a no-op even when timers are disarmed).
- **`flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`** — the fake_async suite opts back into real timers (`timersEnabled: true` at all 6 construction sites) and gained 3 regression tests:
  - `a successful restore stays silent while the user sits on home` (the `_boot` wiring contract pinned above)
  - `the default watchdog arms no timers — nothing left pending` (direct regression for the CI red; pre-fix it fires the restore breadcrumb / dies on the invariant)
  - `timersEnabled: true opts a test-hosted instance back in`

### Files Modified

- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` — `timersEnabled` (test-binding-aware default), `_arm` guard, `_installed` idempotency flag, docs (library + class).
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart` — `_boot()` / `_bootRelay()`: `restoreDone()` at restore completion instead of post-navigation; `finally` kept as failure-path net.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` — `timersEnabled: true` opt-in ×6, +3 regression tests.

### Test Coverage

- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`: **19/19 PASS** (was 16).
- Previously-failing suites re-run locally with the CI shard recipe (`--exclude-tags integration`, non-golden/non-`cli_visual`): `test/boot/` + `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` + `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` → **68/68 PASS** (both formerly-red tests green).
- Full CI-equivalent shard verification (`find test … NR % 2 == shard`, both shards, with `FA_*` shell vars unset — this runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` otherwise leaks into `providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart`, as noted in the PR description): **shard 0: 1786 passed, 91 skipped, 0 failed; shard 1: 1908 passed, 17 skipped, 0 failed.**
- `flutter analyze` on `flutter_app`: no errors.

{"content":"## Validation CI red on `cd2d3f39` — fixed: boot watchdog left pending timers in widget tests + restore phase never disarmed on a healthy boot

### Issues/Notes

- Validation CI failed on head `cd2d3f39` in **both** `Flutter app tests` shards (the `Quality gate` failure is just the aggregate of those two legs). `ci_failures_full.log` was not present locally; root cause was recovered from the failed jobs' logs (run 38364224395, jobs 115185593321 / 115185593401) and reproduced locally (1 failure per shard, same tests).
- Both failures were the flutter_test `!timersPending` invariant — `A Timer is still pending even after the widget tree was disposed`:
  - `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` — "first boot: onboarding → skip → setup → connect → launcher home"
  - `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` — "a restorable connection boots straight to the spinner"
- The pending timer was the watchdog's **restore-phase 10 s timer**, exposed by two defects in the restore-phase wiring (added by the earlier review-thread fix):
  1. `_boot()` disarmed the phase in a `finally` **after** `await navigator.pushReplacement(...)` — that future stays pending for as long as the user sits on home (and `bootExtensionRelay` awaits `onHome`, which awaits the same navigation). So on every **healthy** launch the restore phase stayed armed for the whole session: production would log spurious `restore not completed` breadcrumbs from 10 s after every boot (×10 + a `giving up` line), and widget tests that end parked on home died on the pending timer.
  2. The spinner-shaped test ends **while the restore is intentionally still in flight** — with real watchdog timers inside `testWidgets` boot flows, no disarm placement can save that test; the binding fails any test that ends with timers pending.
- Note: `flutter analyze` on this head is clean (no errors); the two lints in `flutter_app/test/boot/` (unused `fa/main.dart` import — pre-existing on `main`; `fake_async` not a declared dev-dep — info-level, analyze leg already green on CI) are out of scope for this fix.

### Approach

- **`flutter_app/lib/main.dart`** — disarm the restore phase when the *restore* ends, not when the navigation ends: `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` now runs right after `BootSteps.mark('restore:session')` and at the top of `_bootRelay`'s `onHome` (both before the `pushReplacement` await). The `finally` blocks remain as the failure-path net (`restoreDone` is idempotent): a restore that threw — landing on the setup form, no wedge — is still disarmed on the way out, so the review thread's post-frame coverage is unchanged for real wedges and no longer spams healthy launches.
- **`flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart`** — `BootWatchdog` now takes `bool? timersEnabled`, defaulting to "armed everywhere EXCEPT under a `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding`" (same binding-name probe as `app_tile_host.dart`, which documents the identical `!timersPending` failure mode). Under tests the phases are still recorded (`beginRestore`/`restoreDone` bookkeeping, `describe()` context) but no real timer exists — nothing can fire, nothing is left pending. Release builds never run under a test binding, so production always arms. `install()` idempotency now keys on an `_installed` flag (a second install stays a no-op even when timers are disarmed).
- **`flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`** — the fake_async suite opts back into real timers (`timersEnabled: true` at all 6 construction sites) and gained 3 regression tests:
  - `a successful restore stays silent while the user sits on home` (the `_boot` wiring contract pinned above)
  - `the default watchdog arms no timers — nothing left pending` (direct regression for the CI red; pre-fix it fires the restore breadcrumb / dies on the invariant)
  - `timersEnabled: true opts a test-hosted instance back in`

### Files Modified

- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` — `timersEnabled` (test-binding-aware default), `_arm` guard, `_installed` idempotency flag, docs (library + class).
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart` — `_boot()` / `_bootRelay()`: `restoreDone()` at restore completion instead of post-navigation; `finally` kept as failure-path net.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` — `timersEnabled: true` opt-in ×6, +3 regression tests.

### Test Coverage

- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`: **19/19 PASS** (was 16).

{"content":"# Automated review — thread 7 (restore-phase coverage + screenshot scope)

Both key issues from this review are addressed on the current head:

**1. `restore:*` marks were dead weight — watchdog disarmed at the first frame.**
Fixed (option 1) in the previous rework round: `BootWatchdog` has a restore phase (`beginRestore()` → `restoreDone()`, `FA_BOOT_RESTORE_WATCHDOG_MS`, default 10 s), armed in `_BootstrapScreenState._boot()` / `_bootRelay()` and wired around the `restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session` marks, so a post-frame wedge breadcrumbs with the full `BootSteps` context.

This round hardened that same wiring after the validation-CI red it produced (`cd2d3f39`, both flutter-tests shards):

- **Disarm placement** — `restoreDone()` ran in a `finally` AFTER `await navigator.pushReplacement(...)`, which stays pending for as long as the user sits on home. A healthy boot therefore kept the restore phase armed for the whole session (spurious "restore not completed" breadcrumbs from 10 s after every launch) and left the 10 s timer pending at the end of widget tests that park on home. `restoreDone()` now runs the moment the restore completes, before the navigation; the `finally` stays as the failure-path net (`restoreDone` is idempotent). Same fix in `_bootRelay` (`bootExtensionRelay` awaits `onHome`, which awaits the same `pushReplacement`).
- **Arming under `flutter test`** — the two failed shards (`test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` first-boot, `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` boots-straight-to-the-spinner) died on the binding's `!timersPending` invariant: boot flows legitimately end mid-restore or parked on home, so real watchdog timers cannot exist inside `testWidgets`. `BootWatchdog` now takes `timersEnabled` (default: armed everywhere EXCEPT under a `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding` — the same binding-name probe as `app_tile_host.dart`); phases are still recorded, production always arms, and the fake_async suite opts back in with `timersEnabled: true`.

Regression tests: `a successful restore stays silent while the user sits on home`, `the default watchdog arms no timers — nothing left pending`, `timersEnabled: true opts a test-hosted instance back in` (`flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`, 19/19).

**2. 100 golden screenshots under `test/integration/screenshots/` deleted.**
Not present on the current head — the branch diff vs `main` is exactly the 4 PR files (`app_boot.dart`, `boot_watchdog.dart`, `main.dart`, `boot_watchdog_test.dart`); no screenshot deletions remain.

{"content":"## Validation CI red on `cd2d3f39` — fixed: boot watchdog left pending timers in widget tests + restore phase never disarmed on a healthy boot

### Issues/Notes

- Validation CI failed on head `cd2d3f39` in **both** `Flutter app tests` shards (the `Quality gate` failure is just the aggregate of those two legs). `ci_failures_full.log` was not present locally; root cause was recovered from the failed jobs' logs (run 38364224395, jobs 115185593321 / 115185593401) and reproduced locally (1 failure per shard, same tests).
- Both failures were the flutter_test `!timersPending` invariant — `A Timer is still pending even after the widget tree was disposed`:
  - `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` — "first boot: onboarding → skip → setup → connect → launcher home"
  - `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` — "a restorable connection boots straight to the spinner"
- The pending timer was the watchdog's **restore-phase 10 s timer**, exposed by two defects in the restore-phase wiring (added by the earlier review-thread fix):
  1. `_boot()` disarmed the phase in a `finally` **after** `await navigator.pushReplacement(...)` — that future stays pending for as long as the user sits on home (and `bootExtensionRelay` awaits `onHome`, which awaits the same navigation). So on every **healthy** launch the restore phase stayed armed for the whole session: production would log spurious `restore not completed` breadcrumbs from 10 s after every boot (×10 + a `giving up` line), and widget tests that end parked on home died on the pending timer.
  2. The spinner-shaped test ends **while the restore is intentionally still in flight** — with real watchdog timers inside `testWidgets` boot flows, no disarm placement can save that test; the binding fails any test that ends with timers pending.
- Note: `flutter analyze` on this head is clean (no errors); the two lints in `flutter_app/test/boot/` (unused `fa/main.dart` import — pre-existing on `main`; `fake_async` not a declared dev-dep — info-level, analyze leg already green on CI) are out of scope for this fix.

### Approach

- **`flutter_app/lib/main.dart`** — disarm the restore phase when the *restore* ends, not when the navigation ends: `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` now runs right after `BootSteps.mark('restore:session')` and at the top of `_bootRelay`'s `onHome` (both before the `pushReplacement` await). The `finally` blocks remain as the failure-path net (`restoreDone` is idempotent): a restore that threw — landing on the setup form, no wedge — is still disarmed on the way out, so the review thread's post-frame coverage is unchanged for real wedges and no longer spams healthy launches.
- **`flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart`** — `BootWatchdog` now takes `bool? timersEnabled`, defaulting to "armed everywhere EXCEPT under a `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding`" (same binding-name probe as `app_tile_host.dart`, which documents the identical `!timersPending` failure mode). Under tests the phases are still recorded (`beginRestore`/`restoreDone` bookkeeping, `describe()` context) but no real timer exists — nothing can fire, nothing is left pending. Release builds never run under a test binding, so production always arms. `install()` idempotency now keys on an `_installed` flag (a second install stays a no-op even when timers are disarmed).
- **`flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`** — the fake_async suite opts back into real timers (`timersEnabled: true` at all 6 construction sites) and gained 3 regression tests:
  - `a successful restore stays silent while the user sits on home` (the `_boot` wiring contract pinned above)
  - `the default watchdog arms no timers — nothing left pending` (direct regression for the CI red; pre-fix it fires the restore breadcrumb / dies on the invariant)
  - `timersEnabled: true opts a test-hosted instance back in`

### Files Modified

- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` — `timersEnabled` (test-binding-aware default), `_arm` guard, `_installed` idempotency flag, docs (library + class).
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart` — `_boot()` / `_bootRelay()`: `restoreDone()` at restore completion instead of post-navigation; `finally` kept as failure-path net.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` — `timersEnabled: true` opt-in ×6, +3 regression tests.

### Test Coverage

- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`: **19/19 PASS** (was 16).
- Previously-failing suites re-run locally with the CI shard recipe (`--exclude-tags integration`, non-golden/non-`cli_visual`): `test/boot/` + `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` + `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` → **68/68 PASS** (both formerly-red tests green).
- Full CI-equivalent shard verification (`find test … NR % 2 == shard`, both shards, with `FA_*` shell vars unset — this runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` otherwise leaks into `providers_queue_writer_io_test.dart`, as noted in the PR description): **shard 0: 1786 passed, 91 skipped, 0 failed; shard 1: 1908 passed, 17 skipped, 0 failed.**
- `flutter analyze` on `flutter_app`: no errors.
","path":"outputs/response.md"}

{"content":"## Validation CI red on `cd2d3f39` — fixed: boot watchdog left pending timers in widget tests + restore phase never disarmed on a healthy boot

### Issues/Notes

- Validation CI failed on head `cd2d3f39` in **both** `Flutter app tests` shards (the `Quality gate` failure is just the aggregate of those two legs). `ci_failures_full.log` was not present locally; root cause was recovered from the failed jobs' logs (run 38364224395, jobs 115185593321 / 115185593401) and reproduced locally (1 failure per shard, same tests).
- Both failures were the flutter_test `!timersPending` invariant — `A Timer is still pending even after the widget tree was disposed`:
  - `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` — "first boot: onboarding → skip → setup → connect → launcher home"
  - `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` — "a restorable connection boots straight to the spinner"
- The pending timer was the watchdog's **restore-phase 10 s timer**, exposed by two defects in the restore-phase wiring (added by the earlier review-thread fix):
  1. `_boot()` disarmed the phase in a `finally` **after** `await navigator.pushReplacement(...)` — that future stays pending for as long as the user sits on home (and `bootExtensionRelay` awaits `onHome`, which awaits the same navigation). So on every **healthy** launch the restore phase stayed armed for the whole session: production would log spurious `restore not completed` breadcrumbs from 10 s after every boot (×10 + a `giving up` line), and widget tests that end parked on home died on the pending timer.
  2. The spinner-shaped test ends **while the restore is intentionally still in flight** — with real watchdog timers inside `testWidgets` boot flows, no disarm placement can save that test; the binding fails any test that ends with timers pending.
- Note: `flutter analyze` on this head is clean (no errors); the two lints in `flutter_app/test/boot/` (unused `fa/main.dart` import — pre-existing on `main`; `fake_async` not a declared dev-dep — info-level, analyze leg already green on CI) are out of scope for this fix.

### Approach

- **`flutter_app/lib/main.dart`** — disarm the restore phase when the *restore* ends, not when the navigation ends: `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` now runs right after `BootSteps.mark('restore:session')` and at the top of `_bootRelay`'s `onHome` (both before the `pushReplacement` await). The `finally` blocks remain as the failure-path net (`restoreDone` is idempotent): a restore that threw — landing on the setup form, no wedge — is still disarmed on the way out, so the review thread's post-frame coverage is unchanged for real wedges and no longer spams healthy launches.
- **`flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart`** — `BootWatchdog` now takes `bool? timersEnabled`, defaulting to "armed everywhere EXCEPT under a `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding`" (same binding-name probe as `app_tile_host.dart`, which documents the identical `!timersPending` failure mode). Under tests the phases are still recorded (`beginRestore`/`restoreDone` bookkeeping, `describe()` context) but no real timer exists — nothing can fire, nothing is left pending. Release builds never run under a test binding, so production always arms. `install()` idempotency now keys on an `_installed` flag (a second install stays a no-op even when timers are disarmed).
- **`flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`** — the fake_async suite opts back into real timers (`timersEnabled: true` at all 6 construction sites) and gained 3 regression tests:
  - `a successful restore stays silent while the user sits on home` (the `_boot` wiring contract pinned above)
  - `the default watchdog arms no timers — nothing left pending` (direct regression for the CI red; pre-fix it fires the restore breadcrumb / dies on the invariant)
  - `timersEnabled: true opts a test-hosted instance back in`

### Files Modified

- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` — `timersEnabled` (test-binding-aware default), `_arm` guard, `_installed` idempotency flag, docs (library + class).
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart` — `_boot()` / `_bootRelay()`: `restoreDone()` at restore completion instead of post-navigation; `finally` kept as failure-path net.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` — `timersEnabled: true` opt-in ×6, +3 regression tests.

### Test Coverage

- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`: **19/19 PASS** (was 16).
- Previously-failing suites re-run locally with the CI shard recipe (`--exclude-tags integration`, non-golden/non-`cli_visual`): `test/boot/` + `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` + `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` → **68/68 PASS** (both formerly-red tests green).

- `flutter analyze` on `flutter_app`: no errors.

{"content":"## Validation CI red on `cd2d3f39` — fixed: boot watchdog left pending timers in widget tests + restore phase never disarmed on a healthy boot

### Issues/Notes

- Validation CI failed on head `cd2d3f39` in **both** `Flutter app tests` shards (the `Quality gate` failure is just the aggregate of those two legs). `ci_failures_full.log` was not present locally; root cause was recovered from the failed jobs' logs (run 38364224395, jobs 115185593321 / 115185593401) and reproduced locally (1 failure per shard, same tests).
- Both failures were the flutter_test `!timersPending` invariant — `A Timer is still pending even after the widget tree was disposed`:
  - `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` — "first boot: onboarding → skip → setup → connect → launcher home"
  - `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` — "a restorable connection boots straight to the spinner"
- The pending timer was the watchdog's **restore-phase 10 s timer**, exposed by two defects in the restore-phase wiring (added by the earlier review-thread fix):
  1. `_boot()` disarmed the phase in a `finally` **after** `await navigator.pushReplacement(...)` — that future stays pending for as long as the user sits on home (and `bootExtensionRelay` awaits `onHome`, which awaits the same navigation). So on every **healthy** launch the restore phase stayed armed for the whole session: production would log spurious `restore not completed` breadcrumbs from 10 s after every boot (×10 + a `giving up` line), and widget tests that end parked on home died on the pending timer.
  2. The spinner-shaped test ends **while the restore is intentionally still in flight** — with real watchdog timers inside `testWidgets` boot flows, no disarm placement can save that test; the binding fails any test that ends with timers pending.
- Note: `flutter analyze` on this head is clean (no errors); the two lints in `flutter_app/test/boot/` (unused `fa/main.dart` import — pre-existing on `main`; `fake_async` not a declared dev-dep — info-level, analyze leg already green on CI) are out of scope for this fix.

### Approach

- **`flutter_app/lib/main.dart`** — disarm the restore phase when the *restore* ends, not when the navigation ends: `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` now runs right after `BootSteps.mark('restore:session')` and at the top of `_bootRelay`'s `onHome` (both before the `pushReplacement` await). The `finally` blocks remain as the failure-path net (`restoreDone` is idempotent): a restore that threw — landing on the setup form, no wedge — is still disarmed on the way out, so the review thread's post-frame coverage is unchanged for real wedges and no longer spams healthy launches.
- **`flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart`** — `BootWatchdog` now takes `bool? timersEnabled`, defaulting to "armed everywhere EXCEPT under a `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding`" (same binding-name probe as `app_tile_host.dart`, which documents the identical `!timersPending` failure mode). Under tests the phases are still recorded (`beginRestore`/`restoreDone` bookkeeping, `describe()` context) but no real timer exists — nothing can fire, nothing is left pending. Release builds never run under a test binding, so production always arms. `install()` idempotency now keys on an `_installed` flag (a second install stays a no-op even when timers are disarmed).
- **`flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`** — the fake_async suite opts back into real timers (`timersEnabled: true` at all 6 construction sites) and gained 3 regression tests:
  - `a successful restore stays silent while the user sits on home` (the `_boot` wiring contract pinned above)
  - `the default watchdog arms no timers — nothing left pending` (direct regression for the CI red; pre-fix it fires the restore breadcrumb / dies on the invariant)
  - `timersEnabled: true opts a test-hosted instance back in`

### Files Modified

- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` — `timersEnabled` (test-binding-aware default), `_arm` guard, `_installed` idempotency flag, docs (library + class).
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart` — `_boot()` / `_bootRelay()`: `restoreDone()` at restore completion instead of post-navigation; `finally` kept as failure-path net.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` — `timersEnabled: true` opt-in ×6, +3 regression tests.

{"content":"## Validation CI red on `cd2d3f39` — fixed: boot watchdog left pending timers in widget tests + restore phase never disarmed on a healthy boot

### Issues/Notes

- Validation CI failed on head `cd2d3f39` in **both** `Flutter app tests` shards (the `Quality gate` failure is just the aggregate of those two legs). `ci_failures_full.log` was not present locally; root cause was recovered from the failed jobs' logs (run 38364224395, jobs 115185593321 / 115185593401) and reproduced locally (1 failure per shard, same tests).
- Both failures were the flutter_test `!timersPending` invariant — `A Timer is still pending even after the widget tree was disposed`:
  - `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` — "first boot: onboarding → skip → setup → connect → launcher home"
  - `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` — "a restorable connection boots straight to the spinner"
- The pending timer was the watchdog's **restore-phase 10 s timer**, exposed by two defects in the restore-phase wiring (added by the earlier review-thread fix):
  1. `_boot()` disarmed the phase in a `finally` **after** `await navigator.pushReplacement(...)` — that future stays pending for as long as the user sits on home (and `bootExtensionRelay` awaits `onHome`, which awaits the same navigation). So on every **healthy** launch the restore phase stayed armed for the whole session: production would log spurious `restore not completed` breadcrumbs from 10 s after every boot (×10 + a `giving up` line), and widget tests that end parked on home died on the pending timer.
  2. The spinner-shaped test ends **while the restore is intentionally still in flight** — with real watchdog timers inside `testWidgets` boot flows, no disarm placement can save that test; the binding fails any test that ends with timers pending.
- Note: `flutter analyze` on this head is clean (no errors); the two lints in `flutter_app/test/boot/` (unused `fa/main.dart` import — pre-existing on `main`; `fake_async` not a declared dev-dep — info-level, analyze leg already green on CI) are out of scope for this fix.

### Approach

- **`flutter_app/lib/main.dart`** — disarm the restore phase when the *restore* ends, not when the navigation ends: `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` now runs right after `BootSteps.mark('restore:session')` and at the top of `_bootRelay`'s `onHome` (both before the `pushReplacement` await). The `finally` blocks remain as the failure-path net (`restoreDone` is idempotent): a restore that threw — landing on the setup form, no wedge — is still disarmed on the way out, so the review thread's post-frame coverage is unchanged for real wedges and no longer spams healthy launches.
- **`flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart`** — `BootWatchdog` now takes `bool? timersEnabled`, defaulting to "armed everywhere EXCEPT under a `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding`" (same binding-name probe as `app_tile_host.dart`, which documents the identical `!timersPending` failure mode). Under tests the phases are still recorded (`beginRestore`/`restoreDone` bookkeeping, `describe()` context) but no real timer exists — nothing can fire, nothing is left pending. Release builds never run under a test binding, so production always arms. `install()` idempotency now keys on an `_installed` flag (a second install stays a no-op even when timers are disarmed).
- **`flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`** — the fake_async suite opts back into real timers (`timersEnabled: true` at all 6 construction sites) and gained 3 regression tests:
  - `a successful restore stays silent while the user sits on home` (the `_boot` wiring contract pinned above)
  - `the default watchdog arms no timers — nothing left pending` (direct regression for the CI red; pre-fix it fires the restore breadcrumb / dies on the invariant)
  - `timersEnabled: true opts a test-hosted instance back in`

### Files Modified

- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` — `timersEnabled` (test-binding-aware default), `_arm` guard, `_installed` idempotency flag, docs (library + class).
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart` — `_boot()` / `_bootRelay()`: `restoreDone()` at restore completion instead of post-navigation; `finally` kept as failure-path net.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` — `timersEnabled: true` opt-in ×6, +3 regression tests.

### Test Coverage

- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`: **19/19 PASS** (was 16).
- Previously-failing suites re-run locally with the CI shard recipe (`--exclude-tags integration`, non-golden/non-`cli_visual`): `test/boot/` + `test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` + `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` → **68/68 PASS** (both formerly-red tests green).

- `flutter analyze` on `flutter_app`: no errors.

{"content":"# Automated review — thread 7 (restore-phase coverage + screenshot scope)

Both key issues from this review are addressed on the current head:

**1. `restore:*` marks were dead weight — watchdog disarmed at the first frame.**
Fixed (option 1) in the previous rework round: `BootWatchdog` has a restore phase (`beginRestore()` → `restoreDone()`, `FA_BOOT_RESTORE_WATCHDOG_MS`, default 10 s), armed in `_BootstrapScreenState._boot()` / `_bootRelay()` and wired around the `restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session` marks, so a post-frame wedge breadcrumbs with the full `BootSteps` context.

This round hardened that same wiring after the validation-CI red it produced (`cd2d3f39`, both flutter-tests shards):

- **Disarm placement** — `restoreDone()` ran in a `finally` AFTER `await navigator.pushReplacement(...)`, which stays pending for as long as the user sits on home. A healthy boot therefore kept the restore phase armed for the whole session (spurious "restore not completed" breadcrumbs from 10 s after every launch) and left the 10 s timer pending at the end of widget tests that park on home. `restoreDone()` now runs the moment the restore completes, before the navigation; the `finally` stays as the failure-path net (`restoreDone` is idempotent). Same fix in `_bootRelay` (`bootExtensionRelay` awaits `onHome`, which awaits the same `pushReplacement`).
- **Arming under `flutter test`** — the two failed shards (`test/integration/boot_flows_test.dart` first-boot, `test/onboarding_screen_test.dart` boots-straight-to-the-spinner) died on the binding's `!timersPending` invariant: boot flows legitimately end mid-restore or parked on home, so real watchdog timers cannot exist inside `testWidgets`. `BootWatchdog` now takes `timersEnabled` (default: armed everywhere EXCEPT under a `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding` — the same binding-name probe as `app_tile_host.dart`); phases are still recorded, production always arms, and the fake_async suite opts back in with `timersEnabled: true`.

Regression tests: `a successful restore stays silent while the user sits on home`, `the default watchdog arms no timers — nothing left pending`, `timersEnabled: true opts a test-hosted instance back in` (`flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`, 19/19).

**2. 100 golden screenshots under `test/integration/screenshots/` deleted.**
